controls.title: Building Security Risk Management Systems
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA establishes and maintains its security risk management system. It sets out the governance structures, roles, and responsibilities required to manage cybersecurity and information security risks as enterprise-level business risks, in alignment with the NOF Corp Secure SketCH framework.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from department managers and DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Inappropriate or insufficient allocation of resources for security, resulting in unaddressed risks and an ineffective security posture. Inconsistent risk management practices across MCNA where the IT security risk management system fails to align with other organizational risk management systems. Delayed or disorganized incident response due to undefined command-and-control structures, increasing the business impact of security events. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects an undeveloped or incomplete risk management governance system.

clauses.clause_text: Security risk management is governed at the executive level, with the IT-MIS Director serving as the primary accountable owner and the CFO serving as executive sponsor.
Security risks are managed as business risks, on par with compliance, financial, and reputational risks, and are reviewed at the management level.
The relationship between the IT security risk management system and other organizational risk management systems (financial, operational, compliance) is documented and maintained.
Sufficient budget and personnel for security measures and business execution are planned, evaluated at management reviews, and approved annually.
Roles and responsibilities for developing, implementing, and assessing MCNA’s cybersecurity strategy are defined, documented, and communicated to each assigned party.
Work is appropriately divided between internal MCNA staff and outsourced parties (e.g., DIS Computers), with clear delineation of scope.
Conflicting duties and authorities are separated per the principle of segregation of duties.
Security roles and responsibilities for business partners, contractors, and vendors are explicitly defined in contracts or agreements.
A cross-organizational communications framework for cybersecurity is established, involving IT-MIS, executive management, business units, and the MSP (DIS Computers).
Security risks are identified and managed when initiating or managing any project within MCNA, regardless of project type or scale.

The security risk management framework is reviewed at least annually and additionally when triggered by audit results, changes in laws or regulations, or requirements from NOF Corp, customers, or other stakeholders.
Budget and personnel allocations for security are reviewed at least annually as part of the management review process.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Documented roles and responsibilities for security risk management.
Evidence of management-level security risk review (e.g., meeting minutes or decision records).
Approved budget and resource allocations for security.
Completed security risk management framework review record with date and approver.

controls.title: Awareness and Compliance with Laws and Guidelines
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA stays current with the laws, regulations, and standards that apply to its operations, and how it converts those obligations into a documented compliance response. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and any customer- or jurisdiction-driven requirements.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from HR (Legal) and DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Regulatory warnings, fines, or penalties resulting from non-compliance with an applicable law. Loss of customer trust and contract terminations if MCNA cannot evidence compliance posture during a customer audit. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment falls below required thresholds. Reputational harm following an incident discovered to have occurred while MCNA was non-compliant.

clauses.clause_text: An inventory of applicable laws, regulations, and standards is maintained, covering at minimum: U.S. federal and state data protection law, the NOF Corp parent mandate to align with Secure SketCH, and customer-mandated security requirements.
Guidance from regulatory and industry bodies relevant to the metal coatings industry and to MCNA’s U.S. operating jurisdictions is tracked on an ongoing basis.
Alignment with the Secure SketCH framework, which incorporates NIST, ISO, and SOC controls under the parent NOF Corp mandate, is maintained.
Information assets covered by each applicable requirement are identified, and the responsible owner for each is documented.
A documented response policy is established for each applicable requirement; the IT-MIS Director is accountable for technical compliance and the CFO is accountable for executive compliance.

Compliance with all applicable mandatory requirements is maintained; deviations are tracked as risk acceptances approved by the CFO and recorded in the risk register maintained under Standard SSK-02-1.
Coordination with HR (which also handles Legal) takes place on any requirement that has employment, privacy, or contractual implications.
Changes to applicable laws, regulations, and standards are reviewed at least annually, and additionally when new or revised requirements are notified by NOF Corp, customers, or regulators.
A periodic compliance check against the Secure SketCH self-assessment is performed by the IT-MIS Director, with results reported to the CFO.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current inventory of applicable laws, regulations, and standards.
Documented response policy for each requirement.
Most recent Secure SketCH self-assessment results.
Risk acceptances on record for any approved deviations.

controls.title: Establishing and Disseminating the Basic and Overarching Security Policy
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA establishes, approves, communicates, and maintains its overarching information security policy. It ensures that all applicable workers and users understand MCNA’s fundamental stance on protecting information assets from threats, in alignment with the NOF Corp Secure SketCH framework.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from HR (Legal) and DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Ad hoc and inconsistent security measures that prevent MCNA from achieving or demonstrating a coherent security posture. Security violations resulting from lack of awareness rather than intent, where the policy has not been communicated to employees. Regulatory compliance risk where an unapproved or outdated policy fails to reflect current legal requirements. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects absence of a formally approved and disseminated overarching security policy.

clauses.clause_text: MCNA maintains a formal, written MCNA Information Security Policy that articulates the organization’s baseline stance on protecting information assets from threats.
The policy explicitly defines the scope of application, including which employees, contractors, suppliers, and sites it covers.
The policy is reviewed and approved by the CFO prior to issuance or update.
The MCNA Information Security Policy is communicated to all employees and relevant external parties upon establishment or update.
Acknowledgment of the policy is required from employees as part of onboarding and at each annual review cycle.
A summary of MCNA’s security policy stance is published as an external declaration where required by customers, regulators, or NOF Corp.
The policy is reviewed at least annually, and additionally when triggered by material changes in MCNA’s business, new or emerging threats, or regulatory and framework changes.
The policy remains sufficiently practical and realistic to translate into implementable rules and procedures without disrupting business operations.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current approved MCNA Information Security Policy with version history.
Evidence of CFO approval (e.g., signed approval record or documented decision).
Distribution and acknowledgment records for all applicable employees and external parties.
Documentation of most recent policy review date, reviewer, and outcome.

controls.title: Establishing and Maintaining Documented Policies and Procedures
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA develops, approves, communicates, and maintains the operational rules and procedures that translate the overarching MCNA Information Security Policy into actionable controls. It ensures that all security-related workflows are documented, current, and enforceable, in alignment with the NOF Corp Secure SketCH framework.
controls.cadence: At least annually for all instruments, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from relevant department managers, HR (Legal), and DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually for all instruments, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Undocumented or outdated security procedures that leave workflows operating without clear guidance, increasing the likelihood that vulnerabilities go unaddressed and are exploited. Progressive weakening of MCNA’s overall security posture where periodic review fails to address new threats, technologies, or regulatory requirements. Audit findings, penalties, or contract loss where MCNA cannot evidence documented and approved procedures during customer audits or regulatory reviews. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects absence of documented and maintained operational security procedures.

clauses.clause_text: Operational rules and procedures are developed for each major area of information security practice, providing sufficient detail to implement and evidence compliance with the MCNA Information Security Policy.
All rules and procedures are reviewed and approved by the CFO or designated management authority before issuance.
Employees and relevant external parties are informed of and required to adhere to all applicable rules and procedures.
MCNA maintains, at minimum, the following documented instruments:
All rules and procedures are reviewed and revised at least annually.
Rules and procedures are reviewed and updated when triggered by new laws or regulations, emerging technologies (e.g., generative AI), or significant changes to the operating environment.
Findings from audits, security training exercises, and incident response activities are used to inform revisions to relevant rules and procedures.
Compliance with established rules and procedures is periodically verified for all applicable employees and external parties.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current inventory of all rules and procedures with version dates and management approvals.
Evidence of annual review completion for each instrument.
Employee and external party acknowledgment records for applicable procedures.
Documentation of procedure updates resulting from audits, incidents, or regulatory changes.

controls.title: Identification and Evaluation of Security Risk
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA identifies and evaluates cybersecurity and information security risks across its operations. It establishes the process for maintaining an asset inventory, assessing threats, evaluating risk impact, and assigning risk responses. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and enables evidence-based security investment decisions.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and department managers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Security risks that are not fully identified or evaluated, leaving critical systems exposed to unaddressed threats. A security posture that does not reflect current threats, business changes, or newly discovered vulnerabilities. Inconsistent decisions about which risks to mitigate, accept, avoid, or transfer, increasing the likelihood of over- or under-investment in controls. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects an absent or undeveloped risk identification and evaluation process.

clauses.clause_text: MCNA maintains a current inventory of all corporate information assets, including physical devices, information systems, data stores, and intellectual property, with relative priority ratings based on business importance and sensitivity.

Critical systems are identified from both internal perspectives (impact on MCNA's mission and business goals) and external perspectives (potential impact on customers or partners in the event of a business interruption).
Internal and external security threats are identified and documented, including cyber-attacks, malware, human error, and internal fraud scenarios.

Security risks are evaluated using three complementary methods: scenario-based analysis (e.g., unauthorized access, ransomware, insider threat); the C-I-A rubric (confidentiality, integrity, and availability); and item-specific assessment organized by team, system, application, and network.
For each asset identified as requiring protection, the implementation status of applicable countermeasures is tracked and kept current.
Risk tolerance levels are defined and documented in agreement with executive management and aligned with MCNA's business goals and operational context.
Each identified security risk is assigned a response strategy - mitigate, accept, avoid, or transfer - based on its evaluated impact and the established risk tolerance.
Security risk assessments are reviewed and updated at least annually, incorporating the latest threat trends, vulnerability disclosures, and industry intelligence.

New or supplemental risk assessments are performed when major changes occur, including the start of new business activities, changes to business model, significant technology changes, or material organizational restructuring.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current asset inventory with priority ratings and last-reviewed date.
Completed risk assessment records with evaluation scores and assigned response strategies.
Documented risk tolerance thresholds approved by management.
Evidence of annual review completion with date and approver.

controls.title: Planning and Management for Security Risk Response
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA formulates, manages, and evaluates its security risk response plan. It establishes requirements for prioritizing countermeasures, tracking implementation, reporting to management, and ensuring response plans remain current and effective. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and enables accountable, measurable security investment.
controls.cadence: At least annually for full plan review and effectiveness evaluation, with ongoing progress reviews during the planning period.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and department managers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually for full plan review and effectiveness evaluation, with ongoing progress reviews during the planning period.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Security measures implemented inconsistently or incompletely, leaving known risks unaddressed beyond acceptable risk tolerance. Unaddressed risks that cannot be identified in a timely manner, prolonging exposure and increasing potential impact. Security investments whose effectiveness cannot be demonstrated, optimized, or reported to NOF Corp. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects that risk response planning is undeveloped or not regularly reviewed.

clauses.clause_text: Security measures are prioritized using a risk-based approach, accounting for the risk response policy (mitigate, accept, avoid, transfer) assigned to each identified risk.
Cost and time estimates are developed for each planned security measure, enabling comparison of mitigation costs against residual risk exposure.
Cybersecurity insurance options are evaluated to cover potential financial losses from security incidents, including analysis of supplementary services offered by insurers.

A security risk response plan is developed with measurable objectives (e.g., phishing reporting rate, vulnerability response rate) and phased implementation milestones across short-term and medium- to long-term horizons.
Progress against the security risk response plan is reviewed on a regular cadence during the active planning period, with deviations documented and escalated as needed.
The risk identification, assessment, and response process is formally documented and approved by executive management before implementation.

The evaluated impact of active risks and the implementation status of countermeasures are reported to management at least annually, with technical risk factors translated into business impact language.
External audits of the security risk management process are performed at regular intervals or whenever a significant change to the operating environment occurs.
The security risk response plan is reviewed at least annually based on current trends in cyber attacks and the evolving threat landscape.
After each planning period concludes, actions taken are evaluated for effectiveness, and countermeasures are updated based on evaluation results and audit findings.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current security risk response plan with measurable objectives and phased implementation milestones.
Progress tracking records for security measure implementation, including status and completion dates.
Management reports on risk impact and countermeasure status with executive sign-off.
External audit records, findings, and remediation actions.

controls.title: Leveraging Threat Intelligence
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA collects, analyzes, and applies cybersecurity threat intelligence to strengthen its security posture, inform countermeasure decisions, and support incident detection and response. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and ensures MCNA's defenses reflect the current threat environment rather than lagging behind it.
controls.cadence: Protocol reviewed at least annually; collection and analysis activities are ongoing.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers.
controls.status_description: Protocol reviewed at least annually; collection and analysis activities are ongoing.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Security posture gaps against prevailing cyber threat trends, increasing the risk of successful exploits and operational disruption. Limited ability to proactively block known malicious infrastructure, extending attacker dwell time and increasing incident impact. Delayed detection and response during active attack campaigns, amplifying damage to systems and data. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects no defined process for leveraging external threat intelligence.

clauses.clause_text: A documented policy or protocol for the use of threat intelligence defines the purpose, types of information to be collected, and the end-to-end process for collection, processing, analysis, and distribution to relevant parties.
Threat information is gathered from government and authoritative sources (e.g., CISA alerts, FBI InfraGard, NIST NVD) and reputable security portals on an ongoing basis.
Information on cyber attack tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) is collected from information-sharing forums, industry communities, and peer organizations where feasible.
Logs and alerts from internal security equipment - including firewalls, endpoint detection and response (EDR), and email security controls - are collected and reviewed regularly.
External OSINT tools and commercial threat intelligence services are used to supplement internal collection capabilities where justified by risk and cost.
Collected threat intelligence is analyzed to identify potential attack surfaces relevant to MCNA's environment and to determine whether new countermeasures are required.
Indicators of Compromise (IoC) information - such as malicious IP addresses, domains, and file hashes - is integrated into security controls to support prevention, detection, and response.

Where appropriate and permitted, significant incident information (e.g., confirmed malware infections) is reported to public institutions or information-sharing forums to support the broader security community.

The threat intelligence collection, processing, analysis, and sharing process is reviewed at least annually to ensure it remains relevant, effective, and aligned with the current threat landscape and MCNA's operational needs.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Documented threat intelligence policy with defined collection sources, process, and distribution scope.
Records of active intelligence feeds, subscriptions, and forum memberships with renewal dates.
Evidence of IoC integration into security controls (e.g., firewall block lists, EDR indicator feeds).
Incident reporting records to external forums or authorities, where applicable.

controls.title: Establishing Protocol for Disclosure and Communication of Cybersecurity Information
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA discloses its cybersecurity risk management policies and countermeasure status to relevant stakeholders. It establishes who receives security disclosures, what content is shared, through which channels, and on what schedule. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and fulfills MCNA's accountability obligations to NOF Corp, customers, and other stakeholders.
controls.cadence: At least annually, and whenever a material change to security posture or countermeasures occurs.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from HR Director (Legal) and DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, and whenever a material change to security posture or countermeasures occurs.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Reduced stakeholder trust and damage to MCNA's relationship with NOF Corp, customers, and auditors. Stakeholders making uninformed risk decisions, increasing their exposure and MCNA's liability. Audit findings, contract penalties, or regulatory exposure where security disclosure obligations exist under customer agreements or applicable law. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects no defined protocol for the disclosure and communication of cybersecurity risk information.

clauses.clause_text: MCNA identifies and documents the stakeholders to whom cybersecurity risk management policies and countermeasure status should be disclosed, including NOF Corp leadership, customers with security requirements, auditors, and internal executive management.
Standards for the scope, depth, and method of each disclosure type are established, documented, and approved by executive management before disclosure occurs.

The status of MCNA's response to security risk factors is disclosed to relevant stakeholders in a form and through a channel accessible to the intended recipient (e.g., formal reports, briefings, Secure SketCH self-assessment submissions).

Security risk initiative status may be included in management reports, customer security questionnaire responses, CSR or sustainability disclosures, or NOF Corp audit submissions, as appropriate to the audience.
Disclosures describe the status of MCNA's response to risk factors that could hinder achievement of business goals, not merely the existence of a security program.
Disclosed content is reviewed and updated when policies, countermeasures, or the underlying risk posture changes materially.
Disclosure protocols are reviewed at least annually to ensure alignment with current stakeholder expectations, regulatory requirements, and MCNA's evolving security posture.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current disclosure protocol document with defined audiences, scope, and approved content standards.
Records of stakeholder disclosures made, including recipient, date, and content type.
Management approval records for disclosure content.
Evidence of annual review completion with date and approver.

controls.title: Enforcing Cybersecurity and Information Security Controls Across All Group Companies
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA participates in the NOF Corp group security posture and how it sustains a consistent baseline of cybersecurity and information security countermeasures across MCNA U.S. operations. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: MCNA cannot evidence its security posture to NOF Corp, leading to escalation or loss of group standing. Inconsistent controls across sites allow incidents to occur or expand undetected, increasing damage to MCNA and to the NOF Corp shared brand. A weakness at one MCNA site provides a pivot point that affects other group entities, amplifying reputational and financial impact.

clauses.clause_text: MCNA participates in NOF Corp group security assessments and provides the requested status of its cybersecurity and information security countermeasures on the schedule set by the parent.
A checklist that records the status of security measures across MCNA sites is maintained and used as the basis for periodic group reporting.
Outcomes of NOF Corp group reviews and any groupwide directives are tracked through to implementation by the IT-MIS Director.
A minimum security baseline, derived from the Secure SketCH framework, is enforced across all MCNA U.S. sites and any related entities under MCNA's operational scope.
Security levels are differentiated according to the importance of the assets handled at each location and the criticality of the supporting systems.
Where any site or system has not yet reached the minimum baseline, a remediation plan is established by the IT-MIS Director and DIS Computers and tracked to closure.
The status of security measures across MCNA's footprint is reviewed at least annually, with results reported to the CFO and to NOF Corp as required.
The checklist of security measures and the required minimum baseline are updated when the business environment, group structure, or threat landscape changes materially.
Out-of-cycle reviews are triggered by significant organizational change (e.g., acquisition, divestiture, major site relocation) or by a directive from NOF Corp.

controls.title: Security Assessments Before Contracting With Third Parties
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA evaluates the cybersecurity and information security posture of prospective third parties before entering into a contractual relationship, so that risk introduced through the supply chain is identified and addressed up front.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: MCNA enters relationships with third parties whose security posture falls short of MCNA's risk tolerance. Security weaknesses introduced through the supply chain are exploited and translate into operational, financial, or reputational impact for MCNA. MCNA misses the opportunity to leverage prevention and response know-how that peer organizations have already built, duplicating effort and cost on its own.

clauses.clause_text: Cybersecurity and information security selection criteria for third parties are defined and documented before any new commercial relationship is established.

Required compliance levels are calibrated to the criticality of the data, system access, or service provided, with a higher bar applied to third parties that will handle confidential MCNA information or operate against MCNA production systems.
Each prospective third party is evaluated against the documented selection criteria prior to contract execution, and the evaluation outcome is recorded.
Potential security risks and vulnerabilities arising from the engagement are assessed and documented, including data flows, access scope, and dependencies.
Past security incidents involving the third party, and how the third party responded, recovered, and prevented recurrence, are reviewed where the information is available.
Where appropriate, third-party assessment tools or security rating services are used to obtain an objective evaluation of the third party's security posture.

For important third parties (those with access to MCNA production systems, sensitive data, or operational technology), security governance, incident response planning, and contingency planning are evaluated as part of selection.

The selection criteria and the means and methods of evaluation are reviewed at least annually, and additionally when the threat landscape, regulatory environment, or MCNA operating requirements change.

controls.title: Specifying Security Obligations Within Third-Party Contracts
controls.overview: This standard defines the cybersecurity and information security obligations that MCNA includes in its third-party contracts, so that responsibilities, reporting, and end-of-contract handling are unambiguous and enforceable.
controls.cadence: At least annually for active critical contracts, and at every renewal or amendment.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with HR (Legal) and approval from the CFO for material changes.
controls.status_description: At least annually for active critical contracts, and at every renewal or amendment.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Ambiguous division of incident response roles and responsibilities causes delayed or insufficient response. MCNA has no contractual basis to require remediation, audit access, or evidence from a third party that falls short of expectations. End-of-contract obligations are not honored, leaving MCNA data with a former third party or access credentials still active.

clauses.clause_text: Cybersecurity and information security responsibilities and requirements are identified and documented for both MCNA and the contracted third party.
Third-party security responsibilities, roles, and requirements are explicit in contracts, statements of work, or service specifications, and are not deferred to verbal agreement or implied practice.
Contracts require third parties to report serious vulnerabilities discovered during the term of the contract, including those affecting products, services, or shared infrastructure.
Contracts require cooperation in the development of response and recovery plans, including participation in tabletop exercises or response drills where the engagement warrants.
Where a critical product or service vendor maintains a software bill of materials (SBOM), the contract requires the SBOM to be made available to MCNA on request.
End-of-contract provisions cover return of MCNA information, certified disposal of any remaining data, and revocation of access privileges granted during the engagement.

Evidence of acceptable security practices (e.g., self-attestation, conformance to recognized standards, certifications, or third-party inspection results) is requested and retained on file for the contract term.
Contracts include the right to request audits and provide for penalties in the event of false disclosures or failure to respond to audit queries.
Contract terms relating to security are reviewed at periodic renewal or amendment, and at least annually for active critical contracts.

controls.title: Managing Third-Party Security Risks
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA tracks, assesses, and manages the security posture of its third parties on an ongoing basis after contract entry, so that risk introduced through the supply chain is detected and addressed throughout the relationship.
controls.cadence: At least annually for the inventory and required security levels, with continuous monitoring for security events and material findings.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO for framework or rating changes.
controls.status_description: At least annually for the inventory and required security levels, with continuous monitoring for security events and material findings.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Unclear demarcation of responsibilities and management functions between MCNA and a vendor allows gaps in coverage that surface during an incident. Incidents at a third party (e.g., data breach, malware spread) cause secondary impact on MCNA, including exposure of MCNA data or compromise of MCNA systems. MCNA does not detect deterioration in a third party's security posture in time to require remediation, leaving accepted risk in place.

clauses.clause_text: An inventory of all third parties is maintained, recording the role of each party, the services and functions provided, and a criticality rating reflecting their importance to MCNA operations.
Points of contact and security liaisons for each third party are identified and tracked in the inventory.
The data provided to each third party, and how that data is processed and protected, is documented as part of the inventory entry.
An overarching third-party security control framework is established by the IT-MIS Director and approved by the CFO.
Required or expected security levels are defined for each third party in proportion to its criticality to MCNA, and are reflected in contractual terms under Standard SSK-03-3.
The status of security measures of important third parties is assessed periodically using the methods defined under Standard SSK-03-2.
Where a third party's security measures fall short of the required level, MCNA requests improvement or remediation, with timelines proportional to the severity of the gap.
Importance ratings and security evaluations are revisited at least annually, and additionally after any material change in the service or in the third party's organization.
Services provided by third parties are monitored for security events, in coordination with DIS Computers and using MCNA's existing monitoring tooling.
Legal compliance, service updates, and dark-web activity affecting MCNA's third parties are tracked on an ongoing basis, with material findings reported to the CFO.

controls.title: Developing Cybersecurity Talent
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA identifies the skills and competencies required for security-related roles, develops personnel to fill those roles, and keeps training curricula current with evolving technologies and threats. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and ensures MCNA retains the internal capability needed to operate and oversee its security program.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from HR Director (Legal) and DIS Computers.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Inability to retain qualified personnel, increasing dependency on external resources and creating gaps in the internal security program. Inconsistently understood or fulfilled security responsibilities, leaving operational and governance gaps in MCNA's security posture. Impaired ability to respond effectively to incidents, manage audits, or implement required controls due to inadequate investment in security talent development. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects no program for identifying and developing cybersecurity talent.

clauses.clause_text: MCNA defines the security-relevant roles across its organization — including management oversight, strategic governance, and technical practitioner functions — and documents the competencies and skills required for each role.

A policy establishes the direction and requirements for security education and training, enabling personnel in security-related roles to acquire and maintain the skills necessary for their responsibilities.
A medium- to long-term plan for developing security personnel is established, including a career path framework or education roadmap aligned with MCNA's security program needs.
Security education and training activities are executed in accordance with the established policy and roadmap, with completion tracked against defined timelines.

Security reskilling opportunities are available for personnel transitioning into security-adjacent roles, enabling development of specialized security knowledge and supporting continuity of the security program.
Expected competencies, required skills, and training curriculum are reviewed at least annually to remain current with new technologies, emerging threats, and changes to MCNA's security architecture.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Documented role competency framework with defined skills per security role.
Current education roadmap or training plan with timelines and assigned personnel.
Training completion records per employee with dates.
Evidence of annual curriculum review with approver.

controls.title: Integrating Security Throughout Workers' and Users' Lifecycle
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA embeds security responsibilities and obligations into the full employment lifecycle — from pre-hire screening through onboarding, active employment, and separation. It ensures employees understand and commit to their security duties at each stage. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and reduces the risk of insider threat, unauthorized disclosure, and unaddressed policy violations.
controls.cadence: At least annually for full review; also triggered by HR lifecycle events and regulatory changes.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director and HR Director (Legal), with CFO endorsement.
controls.status_description: At least annually for full review; also triggered by HR lifecycle events and regulatory changes.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Immediate, unmitigated risk from new employees who do not understand their security responsibilities on the first day of access. Unenforceable obligations to protect confidential information after separation when NDAs are not executed, increasing trade secret and sensitive data disclosure risk. Reduced deterrent effect from undefined or uncommunicated disciplinary consequences for policy violations, preventing enforceable action. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects no integration of security obligations into the HR and employment lifecycle.

clauses.clause_text: Background screening is conducted for candidates prior to employment, within the bounds of applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and ethical standards.
Employment contracts include explicit clauses defining each employee's cybersecurity responsibilities and obligations as a condition of employment.
Cybersecurity responsibilities and obligations are explained to all new employees during the onboarding process, prior to or concurrent with system access being granted.
Each new employee signs and submits a security pledge during onboarding, acknowledging their security responsibilities; the signed pledge is retained on file.

Penalties for security policy violations are specified in MCNA employment regulations (e.g., employee handbook or code of conduct), communicated to all employees, and enforced through disciplinary action when violations occur.

Departing employees sign a confidentiality agreement or NDA at the time of separation, clarifying their ongoing obligations regarding MCNA's confidential information, trade secrets, and system access.
Signed confidentiality agreements and NDAs from departing employees are retained on file as binding records in accordance with MCNA's records retention policy.
Security responsibilities and obligations across the employment lifecycle are reviewed at least annually to reflect changes in operational needs, applicable law, and the evolving threat landscape.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Employment contracts with embedded security clauses, available for review.
Signed security pledges from current employees on file with HR.
Signed NDAs from departed employees retained per records policy.
Records of disciplinary actions taken for security policy violations.

controls.title: Security Education for Employees
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA delivers security education and training to all employees, regardless of their direct involvement in security operations. It establishes the training policy, required content areas, measurement of effectiveness, and curriculum review requirements. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and reduces incident risk attributable to employee awareness gaps.
controls.cadence: Curriculum reviewed at least annually; training delivered on a recurring basis per policy.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from HR Director (Legal) and DIS Computers.
controls.status_description: Curriculum reviewed at least annually; training delivered on a recurring basis per policy.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Increased likelihood of malware infection via phishing emails, erroneous transmission of sensitive data, and insider fraud due to insufficient security awareness. Inability to identify knowledge gaps before they result in security incidents without measured training effectiveness, leaving preventable vulnerabilities unaddressed. Ineffective awareness investment when training content does not reflect current attack techniques, leaving employees unprepared for the actual threat environment. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects no structured security education program for all employees.

clauses.clause_text: A policy establishes security education and training requirements for all employees, including trigger conditions (e.g., onboarding, role change, annual renewal), expected competency levels, and completion timelines.

Training curriculum covers the following topic areas: security policy awareness and contingency plan procedures; secure information handling including storage, transfer, and disposal of sensitive data; common cyber attack techniques and defensive measures; incident response procedures including how to report suspected incidents; secure authentication practices including multi-factor authentication; insider threat recognition and reporting channels; social engineering attack techniques including phishing, tailgating, and pretexting; and reporting failures in automated processes such as patch management or configuration tools.

Security education and training is delivered to all employees on a recurring basis following the established policy, using formats appropriate to the content and audience (e.g., e-learning, instructor-led sessions, awareness communications).
Incident awareness communications are shared with employees on an ongoing basis to reinforce awareness of real-world security events and their relevance to MCNA's environment.
Employee understanding of security training content is assessed through tests, e-learning assessments, or other structured measurement methods after each training activity.
Assessment results and feedback are provided to trained individuals to support continuous improvement, and employees with identified knowledge gaps receive supplemental training.
Training curriculum and instructional content are reviewed at least annually against current technology trends, emerging cyber threats, and lessons learned from security incidents.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current training policy with trigger conditions, required topics, and completion timelines.
Training completion records for all employees with dates and delivery method.
Assessment results and scores, with records of supplemental training for employees with gaps.
Evidence of annual curriculum review with approver and revision log.

controls.title: Improving Response and Readiness to Email-Based Cyberattacks
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA tests and improves employee readiness to detect and respond to email-based cyberattacks, including phishing, spear phishing, and business email compromise. It establishes requirements for simulated attack exercises, analysis of results, remedial training, technical controls, and a suspicious email reporting system. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and directly reduces the risk of successful email-borne attacks.
controls.cadence: Training content reviewed at least annually; phishing simulations run on a regular cadence (quarterly minimum recommended).
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR Director (Legal).
controls.status_description: Training content reviewed at least annually; phishing simulations run on a regular cadence (quarterly minimum recommended).
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Inability to assess or improve employee preparedness without regular phishing simulations, leaving MCNA exposed to email-borne malware, credential theft, and business email compromise with no measured baseline. Persistent individual vulnerabilities and repeated unsafe behaviors in real-attack scenarios when remedial training is not provided to employees who fail simulations. Increased volume of malicious emails reaching employee inboxes when technical email security controls (anti-spoofing, attachment restrictions) are absent or weak. NOF Corp escalation if the Secure SketCH self-assessment reflects no program for testing and improving employee readiness to email-based cyberattacks.

clauses.clause_text: Simulated phishing and fraudulent business email exercises are distributed to all MCNA employees on a regular cadence to assess preparedness and build awareness of email-based attack techniques.

Simulated exercises are designed to reflect current phishing trends, including spear phishing and business email compromise, with content updated regularly to reflect evolving attacker techniques such as subject line manipulation, sender address spoofing, and domain impersonation.
Results of each phishing simulation are analyzed to identify performance trends, department-level patterns, and the need for targeted training or technical control adjustments.

Employees who click on simulated phishing links, open simulated malicious attachments, or submit credentials in simulated attacks receive remedial or supplementary training promptly following the simulation.

Technical email security measures are evaluated and implemented to reduce attack exposure, including file attachment type restrictions and sender domain spoofing countermeasures (e.g., SPF, DKIM, DMARC).
A system for employees to report and share suspicious emails is established, communicated to all staff, and supported by a defined response process managed by DIS Computers (MSP).

Phishing simulation content and the overall email security training program are reviewed and updated at least annually based on current phishing trends, simulation results, and security incident data.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Phishing simulation schedule with completion records and per-run click and report rates.
Remedial training records for employees who failed simulations, with dates.
Documentation of technical email security control configurations (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, attachment policies).
Evidence of simulation content review and update history.

controls.title: Implementing Physical Security Zoning by Asset Sensitivity
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA classifies its physical workspaces and infrastructure locations into security zones based on the sensitivity of the assets they contain, and how access to and behavior within those zones is monitored. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and protects MCNA’s information assets, manufacturing systems, and personnel from unauthorized physical access.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Unauthorized persons, including outsiders, may infiltrate high-importance locations and cause information leakage, equipment theft, or operational disruption. Security classifications may fall out of date as workspaces change, exposing sensitive assets to inappropriate audiences. Lack of monitoring in sensitive zones eliminates the audit trail needed to detect or investigate physical-security incidents.

clauses.clause_text: Physical locations across MCNA sites are classified into defined security levels (e.g., Public, General Work Area, Restricted, High Sensitivity) based on the intended use of the location and the sensitivity of the assets it contains.
A documented inventory of physical locations and their assigned security level is maintained by the IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers (MSP) for IT infrastructure spaces.
Server rooms, network closets, and any space hosting MCNA information systems or operational technology are classified at the highest applicable security level.
Workspaces are physically segregated by attribute, role, and the type of information handled, separating employees, partner companies, contractors, and visitors as required by zone classification.

Designated locations and equipment (e.g., servers, cabling, network gear) are physically protected from environmental threats including flooding, fire, and unauthorized access, with protections proportional to the assets’ importance.
Surveillance cameras, escort requirements, or other monitoring controls are deployed in locations classified as Restricted or High Sensitivity to record and deter unauthorized behavior.

The security-level classifications and the scope of locations covered are reviewed at least annually, and additionally whenever the layout of working spaces or the nature of work materially changes (e.g., new construction, relocation of IT infrastructure, introduction of remote-work zones).
Findings from each review, including any reclassification of locations, are documented and reported to the CFO.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current inventory of physical locations with assigned security levels.
Site maps or floor plans annotated with zone boundaries.
Surveillance and escort-log records for Restricted and High Sensitivity zones.
Most recent zoning review report and any approved risk acceptances.

controls.title: Implementing Physical Access and Entry Control
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA controls and records physical entry to and exit from its locations, applying authentication strength proportional to the security level of each zone established under Standard SSK-05-1. It ensures that access to sensitive locations is limited to authorized individuals and that an audit trail is preserved to support incident response and compliance review.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with operational input from DIS Computers and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Unauthorized intrusion, information leakage, or theft at high-importance locations may occur without an authentication record sufficient to detect or attribute the activity. Stale or shared credentials enable insider misuse and weaken the link between identity and access. Inadequate logging undermines incident investigations and customer or regulator audit responses.

clauses.clause_text: Authentication mechanisms commensurate with each zone’s security level are implemented at entry and exit points (e.g., keys for general areas, IC cards or PIN-based access for restricted areas, multi-factor or biometric authentication for high-sensitivity areas).
Tailgating and unauthorized entry are explicitly prohibited; users may not allow another person to enter on their credential.
Visitors and contractors are signed in, identified, and escorted in accordance with the destination zone’s security level.
Keys, IC cards, and other physical access credentials are issued, tracked, and inventoried by the IT-MIS Director, with operational support from DIS Computers (MSP).
Unneeded credentials are promptly collected upon role change, termination, or contract end, and access is revoked or invalidated within one business day.
Lost or stolen credentials are reported immediately and revoked or rekeyed without delay; the incident is logged in the access-control records.
Entry and exit events at restricted and high-sensitivity locations are logged, including identity, timestamp, and access point.

Key issuance and key-return events for lock-and-key resources are recorded; IC card and biometric events are retained electronically for at least one year, or longer where required by contract or regulation.
Access logs are reviewed periodically by the IT-MIS Director, with anomalies investigated and recorded.
The lock-and-key management system and the configured authentication methods are reviewed at least annually and updated when zone classifications, technology, or risk posture change.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current credential inventory and revocation records.
Entry and exit logs for restricted and high-sensitivity zones for the most recent retention period.
Most recent log-review report and any anomaly investigations.
Annual review record covering the lock-and-key management system and authentication methods.

controls.title: Physical Management of Endpoints
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA physically manages and protects endpoint devices, including laptops, desktops, smartphones, and tablets, against loss, theft, and unauthorized in-person access. It complements the logical endpoint controls covered elsewhere in MCNA’s standards and supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Unauthorized users may access information at an unattended endpoint, causing information leakage or unauthorized operations. Lost or stolen devices without MDM controls expose corporate data to disclosure and credential compromise. Inconsistent enforcement of clear-desk and clear-screen practices weakens the broader physical-security posture established under Standards SSK-05-1 and SSK-05-2.

clauses.clause_text: Documented rules for the protection of endpoints from loss, theft, and unauthorized access are established and communicated to all users at onboarding and annually thereafter.
A clear-desk and clear-screen practice is enforced: confidential information is not left visible on desks or screens when the user is away or the workspace is unattended.
Users lock their screens whenever leaving their workstation; failure to do so is treated as a policy violation handled with HR.
Automatic screen lock after a defined period of inactivity (not exceeding fifteen minutes) is enforced via centrally managed configuration on all corporate endpoints.
Wire locks or equivalent physical restraints are provided for portable devices used in shared or open workspaces, and storage locations for unassigned or spare devices are kept under lock and key.
Mobile device management (MDM) is deployed on corporate smartphones and tablets to enable remote lock and remote wipe in the event of loss or theft.
Camera and microphone activity indicators are kept enabled so users can detect unauthorized remote operation of communication devices.
Endpoint configuration compliance is monitored centrally, and exceptions are remediated or risk-accepted within a defined timeframe.
Periodic walk-throughs of MCNA workspaces are conducted to visually confirm clear-desk, clear-screen, and physical-security practices are being followed.
The endpoint physical-management rules and supporting solutions are reviewed at least annually, and additionally when remote-work patterns, attack trends, or device technology materially change.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current endpoint physical-management rules and acknowledgment records from users.
Central configuration evidence (screen-lock timeout, MDM enrollment status) for the corporate fleet.
Walk-through reports covering clear-desk, clear-screen, and physical-security practices.
Records of remote lock or remote wipe actions performed on lost or stolen devices.

controls.title: Management of Information Assets
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA classifies, handles, stores, and disposes of its information assets across their full lifecycle (acquisition, use, storage, disposal). It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and ensures that confidential business, customer, employee, and partner information is protected commensurate with its importance.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from HR (Legal) and DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Damage from internal fraud, misconduct, or cyber-attack can be magnified because important information may be removed or tampered with without detection. Failure to meet confidentiality requirements (such as those under trade-secret and similar laws) can prevent legal protection of MCNA’s proprietary technologies, know-how, and other information. Information held beyond its lawful retention period creates unnecessary regulatory and litigation exposure.

clauses.clause_text: Information asset management policies are defined based on the asset lifecycle (acquisition, use, storage, disposal) and applied across MCNA.
Information assets to be protected are identified and assigned an importance level reflecting the impact of an incident (e.g., data leak, falsification, misuse) on internal and external parties.
Permitted scope of use, retention period, ownership, and handling method (storage, disposal, transfer) are defined in proportion to the importance level or sensitivity classification of each asset.
Physical media (paper, removable media) and electronic files are labeled according to their classification.
External media is permitted only when necessary; export-capable endpoints are restricted in line with MCNA endpoint controls under SSK-05-3.
Information disclosed publicly (e.g., on the MCNA website) is reviewed and approved by multiple individuals before release to ensure confidential information is not exposed.
A current inventory of information assets is maintained (in list, ledger, or database form) including importance level, storage location, ownership, and retention metadata.
Activities or interactions with the asset (view, alter, delete, dispose) are recorded for assets where access logging is required by classification.
Information assets are stored in locations appropriate to the data type (e.g., personally identifiable information, financial account data) and segregated from less-sensitive material.
Access to sensitive and other important data is restricted to designated users and systems, and access records are obtained and retained.
Important external storage media and disks are managed under lock and key and/or under a check-in/check-out system that tracks when they are removed and returned.
Logs related to the use of external storage devices are acquired and reviewed periodically by the IT-MIS Director.
Unnecessary data and data that has passed its statutory or contractual protection period is deleted periodically, and the inventory is updated to reflect the disposal.
For critical information, data flow is visualized end-to-end, including any contractor or third-party handling.
When storing important information such as personal information, masking is applied where appropriate to limit exposure.
Asset management policies are reviewed periodically; policy effectiveness is assessed against actual compliance, and gaps are remediated.
Periodic checks (e.g., automated discovery tooling) are performed to surface unmanaged personal or confidential information stored outside approved repositories.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current information-asset inventory with classification, ownership, and retention metadata.
Access logs and external-media check-in/check-out records.
Disposal records and, where applicable, destruction certificates.
Most recent policy review report and any approved risk acceptances.

controls.title: Management of Hardware Assets
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA acquires, tracks, maintains, and disposes of its hardware assets. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and ensures that every device connected to or processing MCNA information is accounted for, protected, and retired in a controlled manner.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Hardware assets that are stolen, lost, or removed in an unauthorized or improper manner cannot be tracked or traced, leading to potential disclosure of MCNA information. Unnecessary hardware left unattended on the company network may become infected with malware and serve as an entry point for attackers. Unsupported devices remaining in service expose MCNA to unpatched vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated.

clauses.clause_text: Hardware-asset management rules are defined and apply to all in-scope device types (IT, IoT, OT, and mobile).
Hardware is procured only from authorized dealers or reputable distributors and is inspected on receipt before being placed into service.
External storage media is restricted to securely managed, organization-approved media; data on such media is encrypted.
All leased or provisioned media and devices are collected at the end of the employee's employment or assignment.
Hardware reaching end-of-support or lacking necessary security features is planned for replacement and/or disposal in advance of the support cutoff.
A management ledger or list is maintained covering all hardware that should be protected by these rules.
Configuration information (OS, network address, owning department, location) is tracked using an IT asset-management system or configuration-management system.
Networks are monitored to detect unauthorized hardware and other unauthorized connections; network-discovery tooling is used to identify all assets connected to MCNA networks.
Issuance and revocation of removable media is tracked in a management ledger.
Inventories of hardware assets are performed periodically; the asset inventory is updated as needed.
Physical presence and ownership of each hardware asset is validated against its inventory record on a defined cadence.

When disposing of storage media, data is completely deleted by writing random values, deleting encryption keys, physically destroying disks, or equivalent means; a disposal or destruction certificate is obtained where required.
When sending a device to a vendor or repair facility for repair or maintenance, the device is verified to contain no important data prior to dispatch.
Hardware-asset management rules, policies, and procedures are reviewed at least annually.
Information about hardware assets is updated periodically and whenever a change occurs, ensuring the inventory is always current.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current hardware-asset inventory with configuration metadata.
Procurement records demonstrating use of authorized dealers.
Network-discovery and unauthorized-device detection reports.
Disposal records and destruction certificates.
Most recent inventory walk-through and reconciliation report.

controls.title: Management of Software Assets
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA tracks, licenses, and controls software installed on its hardware assets. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and ensures that software in use is authorized, supported, properly licensed, and visible to vulnerability management processes.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Vulnerabilities in installed software may go undetected and remain exploitable, exposing MCNA to malware and other threats. Unauthorized or unlicensed software, if undetected, may create copyright-infringement exposure including criminal penalties or claims for damages. License shortfalls can interrupt operations when vendors revoke entitlements or block updates.

clauses.clause_text: Software-asset management rules are defined and apply to all software installed on MCNA hardware.
Software is downloaded only from authorized vendors or trusted distribution sources.
Browsers, mail clients, and the specific versions permitted for use within MCNA are explicitly defined.
Installation of software not on the approved list is prohibited; verification that unauthorized software is not installed is performed periodically.
Software not supported by its vendor is recorded and managed as a documented exception, with a remediation plan and risk acceptance.

An IT asset-management or configuration-management system is used to track software configuration information (name, version, publisher, administrator, installation date) along with vendor support information and the destination hardware asset.
A license-management ledger is maintained to prevent inconsistencies between the number of licenses purchased and the actual install base; over- and under-licensing are remediated promptly.
Software-asset information is updated periodically and whenever a change occurs, so the inventory remains current.
The software inventory is reconciled against installed reality on a defined cadence; discrepancies are investigated and corrected.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current software-asset inventory with version and configuration metadata.
License-management ledger with purchased-vs-installed reconciliation.
Approved-software list and any documented exceptions for unsupported software.
Most recent inventory scan and unauthorized-software detection report.

controls.title: Managing Internal and External Information Systems
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA tracks the full inventory of information systems it operates or relies on, including cloud services and systems owned by individual business units. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and ensures that no system relevant to MCNA business escapes security oversight, regardless of where it is hosted or which department procured it.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, HR (Legal), and Business Sponsors, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Systems that escape the inventory cannot be subjected to security measures, and any neglect of those measures can lead to exploits and actual damage to MCNA or its customers. Shadow IT and unregistered cloud services may store MCNA information outside contractual and regulatory protections. Misclassified criticality may misallocate protection effort, leaving high-impact systems under-defended.

clauses.clause_text: Internal and external systems (including cloud services) for which MCNA is responsible are explicitly defined and recorded.
All information systems used within MCNA, including business-unit-owned systems and shadow IT, are identified and tracked.
Where MCNA provides services to customers, all systems involved in delivering those services are identified and recorded.
System importance is defined using both internal factors (business impact) and external factors (impact on customers during outages).

A current inventory of all information systems is maintained, including the managing or owning department, purpose of use, configuration information (on-premises or cloud), internet connectivity, FQDNs, and IP addresses.
The inventory is validated regularly by auditing each system and its metadata against its inventory entry; discrepancies are corrected.
The MCNA environment is searched periodically for unmanaged or unrecognized systems to maintain inventory accuracy and completeness.
The criteria used to define system criticality, and the criticality assigned to each system, are reviewed regularly and updated as the business changes.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current information-systems inventory with ownership, purpose, hosting model, internet exposure, and criticality.
Records of periodic validation audits and discovery scans.
Procurement-intake records demonstrating new systems are registered before go-live.
Most recent criticality-review report and any approved risk acceptances.

controls.title: Understanding Network Configuration
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA maintains an accurate, current view of its network topology, communication flows, and device configurations. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and ensures that misconfigurations or unauthorized changes can be detected before they enable unauthorized access.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: When the network configuration is not well understood, unexpected misconfigurations or unauthorized changes can lead to unauthorized or improper access to MCNA information from outside the organization. Undetected configuration drift can defeat the controls established by adjacent standards (firewall rules, segmentation, monitoring). Lack of documentation slows incident response and increases the time required to contain a network-borne attack.

clauses.clause_text: A network diagram (variously referred to as a network configuration diagram or network configuration state and flow diagram) is maintained, showing connections between network devices and the systems they serve.
All business-related communications and data flows between users and systems are understood and represented in the documentation.
For each network device or piece of equipment, a record of its configuration rules (permitted inbound and outbound communication) and the business justification supporting those rules is maintained.

Periodic checks are performed to confirm there is no difference between the documented configuration diagram and the actual device configuration or data flow; discrepancies are investigated and reconciled.
Network changes go through a defined change-management process so that the documentation can be updated in step with the production environment.
Detected unauthorized changes are escalated as a security event under MCNA's incident-response process.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current network diagrams covering all MCNA networks.
Device-configuration records with permitted-communication rules and business justifications.
Most recent configuration-verification report and any reconciled discrepancies.
Change-management records linking network changes to documentation updates.

controls.title: Server Configuration Standardization and Hardening
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA establishes, applies, and maintains standardized secure configuration baselines for servers, and how those servers are hardened to reduce the attack surface. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and ensures servers operating MCNA workloads remain in a known-good state across their lifecycle.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Servers operating with default or weakened configurations expose MCNA to compromise via well-known vendor weaknesses, increasing the likelihood and impact of intrusion, ransomware, and data loss.

clauses.clause_text: A standardized secure configuration baseline (hardening baseline) is defined for each MCNA server class (e.g., Windows file server, Linux application server, hypervisor host) and applied at build time.
The hardware and software items and versions composing each MCNA server are inventoried, including operating system, hypervisor, middleware, and key server-resident applications.
Configuration information for each in-scope server is kept current; changes are recorded and the inventory is reviewed at least annually and whenever a material change occurs.

Vendor-supplied or industry-recognized hardening guidance (e.g., CIS Benchmarks, vendor security guides) is used as the basis for MCNA baselines, with deviations documented and approved by the IT-MIS Director.
Unneeded services, ports, default accounts, and sample content are disabled or removed before the server is placed in service.
Administrative access to servers is restricted, logged, and reviewed; shared local administrator accounts are not used in routine operations.
Configuration drift from the approved baseline is detected via automated checks or periodic review and is either remediated or recorded as an approved exception.
Exceptions to the baseline are documented with justification, compensating controls, and an expiry date, and are approved by the IT-MIS Director.
Changes to baselines and to in-scope server configurations follow MCNA's change-management process, including pre-deployment review and post-deployment verification.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current server inventory with class, OS/version, owner, and baseline assignment.
Approved hardening baselines for each server class, including deviation log.
Drift-detection or configuration-audit reports for the most recent review cycle.
Exception register with justification, compensating controls, and expiry dates.
Most recent policy review report and any approved risk acceptances.

controls.title: Endpoint Configuration Standardization and Hardening
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA establishes and enforces standardized secure configuration settings — including hardening baselines — for endpoints (PCs, smartphones, tablets, and equivalent devices) used to access MCNA information. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and reduces endpoint-borne risk to the broader MCNA environment.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
