controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Endpoints operating with weakened or non-standard configurations are commonly the initial foothold for malware, phishing-driven compromise, and lateral movement, magnifying the impact of any single user error.

clauses.clause_text: A standardized secure configuration baseline is defined for each MCNA endpoint class (Windows PC, macOS PC, iOS device, Android device) and applied at build/enrollment time.
Each MCNA endpoint is enrolled in MCNA's endpoint management tooling so that the approved baseline can be applied, monitored, and updated centrally.
Vendor-supplied or industry-recognized hardening guidance is used as the basis for MCNA endpoint baselines; deviations are documented and approved by the IT-MIS Director.
Local administrative privileges on endpoints are restricted; standard users do not operate with persistent local-admin rights.
Disk encryption is enabled on all MCNA endpoints capable of supporting it, in line with MCNA endpoint controls under SSK-05-3.
Endpoint protection (anti-malware/EDR), host firewall, and screen-lock timeout are enabled per the baseline and not disabled by end users.
Removable-media use on endpoints is restricted in line with MCNA endpoint controls under SSK-05-3.
Mobile devices used for MCNA work require a screen-lock passcode/biometric, are configured to allow remote wipe, and apply the approved mobile baseline.
Endpoint compliance with the approved baseline is monitored via the management tooling; non-compliant devices are flagged and remediated or quarantined.
Exceptions to the endpoint baseline are documented with justification, compensating controls, and an expiry date, and are approved by the IT-MIS Director.
Changes to endpoint baselines follow MCNA's change-management process, including pre-deployment validation and staged rollout.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current endpoint inventory with class, OS/version, assigned user, and baseline status.
Approved endpoint hardening baselines, including deviation log.
Compliance reports from MCNA's endpoint management tooling for the most recent review cycle.
Exception register with justification, compensating controls, and expiry dates.
Most recent policy review report and any approved risk acceptances.

controls.title: Restriction of Unauthorized Software on Endpoints
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA restricts the installation and execution of unauthorized software on endpoints (PCs, smartphones, tablets, and equivalent devices). It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and complements MCNA's software-asset and endpoint-management standards.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Unauthorized software on endpoints can introduce malware, expose MCNA data through unvetted cloud sync, breach licensing obligations, and create unmanaged attack paths into MCNA's environment.

clauses.clause_text: An approved-software list (or equivalent allow-list) is defined and maintained for MCNA endpoints, aligned with the software-asset inventory under SSK-06-3.
End users do not install software on MCNA endpoints outside of approved channels (managed software portal, packaged deployment, or explicit IT-MIS authorization).
Local-admin rights on endpoints are restricted so that standard users cannot install or modify software outside approved channels.
On mobile endpoints, app installation is constrained to approved app-store sources or to apps deployed via MCNA's mobile management tooling; sideloading is not permitted on managed devices.
Unauthorized software discovered on an MCNA endpoint is removed or blocked, and the event is logged and reviewed.
Software requested outside the approved list is reviewed for security, licensing, and business need before approval; approved additions are recorded in the software-asset inventory.
Exceptions (e.g., specialist tools needed for a defined task) are documented with justification, compensating controls, scope of users, and an expiry date, and are approved by the IT-MIS Director.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current approved-software list and supporting software-asset inventory.
Endpoint reports showing installed software vs. the approved list.
Log of unauthorized-software detections and the corresponding response actions.
Exception register with justification, compensating controls, and expiry dates.
Most recent policy review report and any approved risk acceptances.

controls.title: Network Device Version Management
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA manages the firmware and software versions of network devices and how it installs the latest stable version when updates are available. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and complements MCNA's network-configuration standard under SSK-06-5.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Network devices left on outdated or end-of-support firmware are a recurrent point of compromise for ransomware operators and intruders, and a single weak device can expose the entire MCNA environment to lateral movement.

clauses.clause_text: Each MCNA network device is recorded in the asset inventory, including model, role, location, and current firmware/software version.
Vendor advisories and end-of-support notices for in-scope network devices are monitored on an ongoing basis.
A target firmware/software version is defined for each device class, reflecting the latest stable version supported by the vendor and validated by MCNA.
Devices that have reached end-of-support, or that cannot be upgraded to the target version, are tracked and prioritized for replacement.
Firmware/software updates are validated in a non-production setting (lab, staging, or pilot device) before broad deployment, where the device class permits.
Updates are deployed under MCNA's change-management process, with rollback steps defined and a maintenance window agreed in advance.
Critical security updates affecting MCNA network devices are scheduled for accelerated deployment, with timeline based on MCNA's vulnerability-management process under SSK-07-5.

Exceptions (e.g., a device that must remain on an older version pending replacement) are documented with justification, compensating controls, and an expiry date, and are approved by the IT-MIS Director.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current network-device inventory with model, role, and version.
Target-version register and end-of-support tracker.
Change records and test/validation evidence for the most recent update cycle.
Exception register with justification, compensating controls, and expiry dates.
Most recent policy review report and any approved risk acceptances.

controls.title: Vulnerability Management Process
controls.overview: This standard defines MCNA's process for identifying, assessing, and dealing with vulnerabilities in its systems and applications. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and integrates with MCNA's configuration, endpoint, software-asset, and network standards.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Without a defined vulnerability-management process, MCNA cannot demonstrate that known weaknesses are being identified and addressed, exposing the company to preventable compromise via vulnerabilities for which patches or mitigations already exist. Inconsistent assessment and prioritization can result in critical, internet-facing vulnerabilities remaining open for extended periods, which auditors, customers, and regulators routinely treat as a material control failure.

clauses.clause_text: Vulnerabilities are identified through a defined combination of authenticated scanning, vendor advisories, threat-intelligence feeds, and reports from MCNA personnel and DIS Computers.
The scope of in-scope assets for vulnerability identification is documented and reconciled against the asset inventories under SSK-06-2 and SSK-06-3.
All identified vulnerabilities are recorded in a single tracking register that captures asset, source, date identified, and current status.
Externally reported vulnerabilities (including those from third parties or researchers) follow the same intake path as internally identified findings.
Each vulnerability is assessed against MCNA's environment, considering severity (e.g., CVSS), exposure (internet-facing vs. internal), and the importance of the affected information assets.
A prioritization scheme is defined that maps the assessed risk to a remediation timeline, with shorter timelines for higher-severity, higher-exposure findings.
Critical or actively exploited vulnerabilities affecting in-scope MCNA systems are escalated immediately to the IT-MIS Director for accelerated handling.
Each vulnerability is dealt with through one of: patching/upgrading, configuration change, compensating control, or formal risk acceptance — and the outcome is recorded in the tracking register.
Risk acceptances are time-bound, documented with justification and compensating controls, and approved by the IT-MIS Director (or the CFO for material residual risk).
Remediation progress against agreed timelines is reported to the IT-MIS Director on a defined cadence; overdue items are reviewed and re-prioritized.
Lessons learned from significant vulnerabilities (e.g., recurring root causes, gaps in baselines or scanning coverage) feed back into the relevant SSK-07 sub-standards.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current vulnerability tracking register, including status, owner, and remediation timeline.
Most recent authenticated-scan reports and reconciliation against the asset inventory.
Risk-acceptance register with justification, compensating controls, and expiry dates.
Reporting artefacts (status reports, dashboards) presented to the IT-MIS Director and CFO.
Most recent policy review report and any approved risk acceptances.

controls.title: Penetration Testing
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA plans, executes, and follows up on penetration tests against its systems and applications. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and is intended to validate, and complement, MCNA's preventive and detective controls.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Without periodic adversarial testing, MCNA cannot reliably demonstrate that its preventive and detective controls work as intended; latent weaknesses chained together by an attacker can lead to outcomes that scanning and configuration review alone do not surface.

clauses.clause_text: Penetration tests are scoped against MCNA assets that are material to confidentiality, integrity, or availability of MCNA information, with priority given to internet-facing systems and systems handling sensitive data.
Each penetration test has a documented scope, rules of engagement, communication plan, and authorization signed by the IT-MIS Director before testing begins.

Testers are demonstrably qualified (relevant certifications, references, or prior engagements) and are bound by confidentiality and data-handling obligations consistent with MCNA's third-party requirements under SSK-03.
A defined cadence for penetration testing is established (at minimum, periodic testing of in-scope environments) with additional tests triggered by significant change.
Tests are executed within the agreed scope and rules of engagement; deviations are escalated to the IT-MIS Director and recorded.
Findings are delivered in a written report that includes severity, exploitation evidence (where appropriate), and recommended remediation.
Findings are entered into MCNA's vulnerability tracking register under SSK-07-5 and follow that standard's prioritization and remediation process.
Remediation of significant findings is verified through retesting or equivalent evidence before the finding is closed.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Penetration-testing schedule and most recent scope/authorization documents.
Tester qualifications and confidentiality/data-handling agreements.
Most recent penetration-test reports and the corresponding entries in the vulnerability tracking register.
Retest or remediation-verification evidence for closed findings.
Most recent policy review report and any approved risk acceptances.

controls.title: Creating and Provisioning Access and Accounts, and Conducting Access Inventory
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA establishes a defined process for creating, provisioning, and inventorying access and accounts across MCNA systems. It supports the parent NOF Corp mandate to align with the Secure SketCH framework and ensures that account creation, modification, and removal occur in a controlled, auditable manner.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and HR (Legal), and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: A high-privilege account that can access important information may be created without approval, potentially leading to information leaks. Stale or orphaned accounts left enabled after staff departures provide low-friction footholds for credential abuse and lateral movement. Shared IDs prevent attribution, weakening MCNA's ability to investigate misuse and to demonstrate accountability to auditors and customers.

clauses.clause_text: Accounts (user, service, and administrative) are issued only in adherence to MCNA's documented account-provisioning protocol, including a recorded business justification and approver.
Accounts are issued at the appropriate access tier (general access, high-level access, privileged access) commensurate with the requested business need; tier assignment is recorded.

Use of shared IDs is avoided; access is managed through individual accounts wherever the system supports per-user accounts. Any shared account that must be retained is documented with justification, owner, and compensating controls.

An expiration date is set for accounts at the time of issuance where the system supports it (e.g., contractor and time-bounded accounts); permanent accounts are subject to the inventory process under SSK-08-1.10.
Account IDs are not reused for a defined period after destruction, so that audit trails can be unambiguously tied to the original holder.
Accounts are promptly disabled or deleted following HR transfer or separation, ideally via an automated synchronization with MCNA's HR system (or other authoritative source of truth).
Accounts that are not used for a defined period are automatically disabled or removed via the relevant system's mechanism, where supported.
When an account is being deleted, it is first deactivated for a defined retention period before full deletion, so that an audit trail of historical activity remains attributable.
A current list of user, service, and administrative accounts is maintained for each in-scope system, integrated with the asset inventories under SSK-06.
An account inventory is performed at least quarterly across in-scope systems; findings (orphaned, over-privileged, or stale accounts) are remediated and recorded.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current account-provisioning protocol (with approver matrix and tier definitions).
Most recent account inventory output across in-scope systems, with remediation status.
HR-to-IT joiner/mover/leaver synchronization records or equivalent control evidence.
Exception register for shared or non-expiring accounts, with justification and compensating controls.
Most recent policy review report and any approved risk acceptances.

controls.title: Authenticating Accounts
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA authenticates users and accounts when they access systems used for business purposes. It establishes the controls that prevent unauthorized access by ensuring every account is verified by an appropriate authentication method, that authentication failures are detected and contained, and that authentication methods are kept current as risks evolve.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Unauthorized access to MCNA systems and information by individuals who are not entitled to use them, leading to information leakage, fraud, or operational disruption. Compromise of administrative accounts, allowing an attacker to escalate privileges, disable controls, or move laterally across MCNA infrastructure. Failure of NOF Corp, customer, or regulator audits where authentication coverage, MFA, or lockout controls cannot be evidenced. Reputational and contractual harm following an incident where weak or absent authentication is identified as a contributing factor.

clauses.clause_text: All users are authenticated before being granted access to any MCNA system used for business purposes. Anonymous or unauthenticated access to systems holding business data is not permitted.

The authentication method used for each system is chosen to match the security risk associated with that system and the business activity it supports. Higher-risk systems (administrative consoles, financial systems, externally exposed services, systems holding confidential data) require multifactor authentication; lower-risk systems may rely on single-factor authentication managed through the central identity provider.

The authentication system in use for each MCNA system is documented and tracked. The IT-MIS Director maintains an inventory that records, for each system: the authentication system, the authentication factors required, the account types supported, and whether the system is integrated with the central identity provider.

When a general-level account experiences repeated failed authentication attempts, the account is automatically locked and the administrator is notified. Lockout thresholds, lockout duration, and notification routing are configured in the central identity provider and reviewed annually.

When an administrative account experiences a failed authentication attempt, the administrator is notified; on repeated failures the administrative account is automatically locked. Administrative account lockout thresholds are stricter than those used for general accounts.
During password authentication, entered passwords are masked on screen (asterisks or equivalent) and are not displayed in plaintext, written to logs, or echoed in error messages.

Authentication is centralized to the smallest practical number of authentication systems. New systems are integrated with the central identity provider (Active Directory / Entra ID) by default; standalone authentication is permitted only by exception, with the exception recorded and approved by the IT-MIS Director.

Where Single Sign-On is implemented, authentication protocols are configured in conformance with current guidelines and best practices for the protocol in use (SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT). Identity assertions are properly generated, transmitted over encrypted channels, and verified by relying systems before access is granted.

Authentication methods in use across MCNA systems are reviewed at least annually by the IT-MIS Director. The review confirms that each system's authentication method remains appropriate for its risk profile and that controls in clauses 08-2.1 through 08-2.8 remain effective.

The technical implementation of authentication protocols is reviewed against current guidance from the protocol authorities and from NOF Corp, customers, or regulators when new or updated guidance is issued. Identified gaps are added to the IT-MIS work plan with a remediation owner and target date.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current inventory of MCNA systems and the authentication method, factors, and integration status for each.
Central identity provider configuration showing lockout thresholds, MFA enforcement, and administrator notification routing.
SSO configuration records (SAML / OAuth / OIDC / JWT) for each integrated system.
Annual authentication-method review record signed by the IT-MIS Director.
Risk acceptances on record for any approved deviations or standalone authentication exceptions.

controls.title: Managing Access Privilege
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA assigns, maintains, and reviews account access privileges. It implements the principles of least privilege and separation of duties, ensures privileges track employee status changes, and requires periodic inventory so that access in effect reflects actual business need.
controls.cadence: Quarterly inventory and review of privileges in effect; annual review of this standard.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and System Owners, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Quarterly inventory and review of privileges in effect; annual review of this standard.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Information leakage when accounts retain access beyond their business need or after employment ends. Fraud or operational error when separation-of-duties violations allow a single account to initiate and approve the same transaction. Audit failure (NOF Corp, customer, regulator) where MCNA cannot evidence quarterly access reviews. Lateral-movement amplification during an incident when over-privileged accounts give attackers a wider blast radius.

clauses.clause_text: Access privileges are assigned only through the documented access-rights assignment process. Ad-hoc grants outside this process are not permitted.
Access control policies and allocation processes are based on the principles of least privilege (PoLP) and separation of duties (SoD). Conflicting roles are not assigned to the same account.
Access to each system and to each information asset is allowed or restricted to match the privilege assigned, so that an account can act only on the resources its privilege covers.

Access privileges are updated immediately in response to HR events — separation (voluntary or involuntary), transfer of department, transfer of role, change in employment status, and onboarding. Where practical this is integrated with the HR system; where not integrated, HR notifies IT-MIS and DIS Computers within one business day of the event.

An inventory of access privileges is performed at least once each quarter and covers every system within scope. The inventory is performed by the IT-MIS Director with support from DIS Computers and from the system owner.
The quarterly inventory is reviewed for excessive, dormant, or obsolete privileges. Any privilege that is not justified is revoked, and the revocation is recorded in the inventory record.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Documented access-rights assignment process.
Quarterly inventory records, signed by the IT-MIS Director.
Records of additions, modifications, and revocations driven by HR events.
Risk acceptances on record for any approved least-privilege or separation-of-duties deviations.

controls.title: Establishing and Adopting Password Policies
controls.overview: This standard defines MCNA's password policy and how it is enforced. It establishes password strength tiered to access level, controls the issuance and initial state of passwords, prevents reuse and cross-system use, and requires periodic policy review.
controls.cadence: Annual policy review; password-policy compliance is verified during the quarterly access inventory under Standard SSK-08-3.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Annual policy review; password-policy compliance is verified during the quarterly access inventory under Standard SSK-08-3.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Unauthorized access through brute-force, credential-stuffing, or password-spray attacks against weak passwords. Cascading compromise when a password reused across systems is disclosed in a third-party breach. Audit failure where MCNA cannot evidence a documented and enforced password policy. Standing exposure on systems retaining vendor-default passwords past go-live.

clauses.clause_text: A password policy is established and documented. The policy specifies minimum length, character composition, history depth, lockout coupling, and update frequency.

Password strength is tiered to the security requirement level of the account: privileged access, high-level access, and general access each have explicitly defined strength requirements. Higher-tier accounts have stricter requirements.

Where multifactor authentication is not available for a privileged account, the password strength requirement for that account is increased above the standard privileged-access tier and the deviation is recorded in the inventory maintained under Standard SSK-08-2.

When a password is communicated to a user, the recipient's identity is verified before the password is delivered. Out-of-band delivery (a different channel from the channel used to request) is preferred.
Any temporary password issued at account creation or reset is treated as one-time and the user is required to change it on first authentication.
Vendor-supplied default passwords on new systems, devices, and applications are changed before the system is placed into productive use.
Password history is enforced so that a user cannot reuse a recent password. The number of historical passwords retained is set in the password policy.
Users do not reuse the same password across MCNA systems. Where Single Sign-On is in use, the SSO password is distinct from any local-account password the user holds.

Where systems support technical enforcement of the password policy, that enforcement is configured and verified. Where a system cannot enforce the full policy technically, compensating controls (monitoring, attestation, scope reduction) are documented.
The password policy is reviewed at least annually, and additionally when authentication-related guidance is updated or an incident indicates the policy is insufficient.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current password policy document, version-controlled.
Identity-provider configuration showing enforcement settings.
Records of compensating controls where enforcement is not technical.
Annual review minutes signed by the IT-MIS Director.

controls.title: Monitoring and Responding to Unusual Access
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA monitors account activity for unusual behavior, alerts administrators, contains compromised accounts, and reviews the definition of "unusual" so it remains effective as business patterns and threats evolve.
controls.cadence: Annual review of the definition of unusual behavior; quarterly review of detection volume and false-positive rate.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and System Owners.
controls.status_description: Annual review of the definition of unusual behavior; quarterly review of detection volume and false-positive rate.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Cyber attacks and insider misuse going undetected, leading to information leakage or operational disruption. Compromised accounts remaining active long enough to allow lateral movement and data exfiltration. Audit failure where MCNA cannot evidence ongoing detection of anomalous account behavior. False positives consuming triage capacity and eroding trust in alerts when the definition of unusual is not maintained.

clauses.clause_text: A definition of unusual account behavior is established and documented. The definition covers, at minimum: logins outside normal business hours for the account's role, unusually long active sessions, geographically improbable logins, repeated authentication failures, and login attempts against disabled accounts.
The definition of unusual behavior is reviewed periodically (at least annually) and after any change in business hours, work patterns, or technology that would alter the baseline.

Administrators are notified when an account they govern shows unusual behavior — long active session, login outside normal business hours, or any other criterion in the definition. Notifications include sufficient context (account, system, time, source) to permit triage.
Account behavior is monitored on an ongoing basis, in real time where feasible and otherwise via near-real-time log review. Accounts confirmed to show malicious behavior are suspended.
Where the central identity provider supports it, behavior analytics (UEBA) is enabled to detect anomalous user activity and surface insider-threat indicators.
Authenticated sessions are forcibly logged off or disconnected after a period of inactivity. Inactivity thresholds are documented in the central identity provider and reviewed annually.
Login attempts against disabled accounts are detected and alerted. Such attempts are treated as potential indicators of compromise and triaged.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current definition of unusual account behavior, version-controlled.
Configuration of monitoring and behavior-analytics tooling.
Records of detections, triage outcomes, and any account suspensions.
Annual review minutes signed by the IT-MIS Director.

controls.title: Implementing a Process Governing the Use of Privileged Accounts
controls.overview: This standard defines how privileged accounts are issued, recorded, protected, and reviewed at MCNA. It enforces individual accountability, multifactor authentication for privileged use, and a documented application/approval process so that elevated access is always traceable to a specific person and a specific request.
controls.cadence: Quarterly review of privileged-account assignments; annual review of the application/approval process and of this standard.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and System Owners, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Quarterly review of privileged-account assignments; annual review of the application/approval process and of this standard.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Untracked privileged access enabling actions on systems without organizational visibility. Account takeover at the privileged tier producing the largest possible blast radius — full system compromise, data exfiltration, or destructive action. Audit failure where MCNA cannot evidence individual accountability, multifactor enforcement, or a defensible approval trail for privileged use. Standing-privilege drift, where privileges granted for past projects remain in effect long after they are needed.

clauses.clause_text: Privileged accounts are issued to individuals, not to groups or shared mailboxes. Each privileged account is traceable to one named person who is accountable for its use.

Privileged accounts are issued only through a documented application/approval process. The application identifies the requester, the systems and operations the account will perform, the business reason, and the requested duration. Approval is recorded and retained.

Multifactor authentication is required for every privileged account. Where a system cannot accept multifactor authentication, the account operates only via a privileged-access workstation or jump host that enforces multifactor authentication at the perimeter, and the deviation is recorded as a risk acceptance.

A central inventory of privileged accounts is maintained. The inventory records, for each account: holder, scope of privilege, system, multifactor-authentication status, approval reference, and last-review date.

For each business application in scope, the privileged user roles and the actions each role is permitted are defined and documented. Role definitions are kept aligned with the application's actual configuration.

The application/approval process is reviewed at least annually. The review confirms that records are complete, that approvals were issued by an authorized approver, and that the issued privileges match the approved request.
Privileged-account assignments are reviewed at least quarterly. Accounts no longer needed are revoked; accounts whose scope no longer matches business need are reduced.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Documented application/approval process for privileged accounts.
Central privileged-account inventory.
Approval records for active privileged accounts.
Quarterly assignment-review records and annual process-review record, signed by the IT-MIS Director.
Multifactor-authentication configuration evidence and any approved deviations.

controls.title: Prior Approval for Privileged Access, and Reconciling Activity Logs Against Approved Scope
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA controls privileged work in production environments. Privileged operations require prior approval, are performed against a defined scope and predefined steps, are recorded in detail, and are reconciled after the fact against the approved request so that any out-of-scope action is detected.
controls.cadence: Per-session reconciliation against the approved request; annual review of the reconciliation process and of this standard.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and System Owners, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Per-session reconciliation against the approved request; annual review of the reconciliation process and of this standard.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Fraudulent or erroneous privileged activity going undetected when no approval baseline exists to reconcile against. Inability to investigate ex post facto when operation records are incomplete or absent. Audit failure where MCNA cannot evidence a defensible approval-and-reconcile control over privileged production work. Insider risk when privileged operations are performed alone with no operational record and no second pair of eyes.

clauses.clause_text: Privileged workers and the privileged access they hold are identifiable at all times. Privileged actions can be attributed to a specific person.

Use of shared IDs is eliminated wherever practical, and access is managed through individual accounts. Where elimination is not possible, the shared ID is recorded in the inventory under Standard SSK-08-6 and access through it is gated by clause 08-7.3.

Where a shared privileged account cannot be eliminated, just-in-time (JIT) access is used: credentials or access are provisioned for each session of use, are time-bound, and the provisioning event is recorded.

Privileged operations against production are requested and approved in advance. The request specifies the operator, the system, the operation, the data scope, the planned timing, and the rollback plan. The approval is recorded.
Privileged operations are performed against predefined steps. Operators do not improvise outside the approved steps; deviations require a new approval before continuing.

An operation record is captured for every privileged production session — at minimum command logs, and where the work is performed via a graphical interface, screen recording. Records are retained per the records-retention schedule.

Production-environment operations are performed under the presence of multiple people where the operation is high-risk (data correction, schema change, security configuration change, or any change with broad user impact). The identity of all attending personnel is recorded.

Access, create, edit, delete, and read-out operations against production data are logged. Logs are protected from tampering by the operator and are retained for the period required by the records-retention schedule.

Where privileged work is performed by remote access, the workers and tasks permitted are defined in advance and controlled by technical means (privileged-access workstations, jump hosts, session recording). Ad-hoc remote privileged access is not permitted.

After each privileged production session, the operation log is reconciled against the approved request. Any operation outside the approved scope is treated as a control event, investigated, and reported to the CFO.

The reconciliation process is itself reviewed at least annually for efficiency and effectiveness. Friction that drives operators to skip steps is addressed; gaps that allow out-of-scope activity to go undetected are closed.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Approved request records for privileged production operations.
Operation records (command logs and screen recordings) for each session.
Reconciliation records linking each session to its request and noting any out-of-scope action.
Annual reconciliation-process review record, signed by the IT-MIS Director.
Records of multi-person attendance for high-risk operations.

controls.title: Encryption of Data in Transit
controls.overview: This standard establishes MCNA's requirements for encrypting data while it is in transit across networks. It ensures that communication channels — internal and external — use verified encryption methods to protect data from interception, eavesdropping, and tampering.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Eavesdropping on or tampering with network communications, leading to data exposure or integrity loss. Regulatory penalties or customer audit failures resulting from unencrypted transmission of sensitive data. Compromise of authentication credentials intercepted over unencrypted channels. NOF Corp escalation if Secure SketCH self-assessment scores decline due to unaddressed encryption gaps.

clauses.clause_text: An inventory of communication data (data in transit) that requires encryption is maintained, and an encryption policy covering procedures and approved methods is documented.
Only encryption methods (algorithms, protocols) that have been verified and certified by recognized standards bodies are used for data-in-transit protection.
Data communication and network traffic are encrypted in accordance with the documented encryption policy.
Data sent externally via email or cloud storage is encrypted before or during transmission.
Publicly exposed systems enforce encrypted communication (e.g., HTTPS with current TLS versions).
Account names and authentication credentials are encrypted when transmitted over any network.
Remote-access connections use encrypted communication channels (e.g., VPN with approved encryption).
Confidential information and backup files are encrypted when transferred or forwarded between systems or locations.
All control-plane and management communication for network devices uses encrypted channels.
Wireless communication is encrypted using AES-based protocols or equivalent.
Encryption algorithms in use are regularly reviewed against published vulnerability disclosures and compromise reports; compromised algorithms are retired on a documented schedule.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Documented encryption policy and inventory of encrypted communication channels.
Configuration evidence showing TLS/HTTPS enforcement on publicly exposed systems.
VPN and wireless encryption configuration records.
Results of the most recent encryption algorithm review.

controls.title: Encryption of Data at Rest
controls.overview: This standard establishes MCNA's requirements for encrypting data at rest — information stored on endpoints, servers, external media, and backup systems. It ensures that stored data is protected against unauthorized access even if physical or logical access controls are bypassed.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Unauthorized access to sensitive data on lost, stolen, or decommissioned devices or media. Information leakage from unencrypted backups or file shares; leaked data cannot be recalled after exposure. Regulatory penalties or customer audit failures resulting from plaintext storage of protected data. NOF Corp escalation if Secure SketCH self-assessment scores decline due to unaddressed encryption gaps.

clauses.clause_text: An inventory of data at rest that requires encryption is maintained, and an encryption policy covering procedures and approved methods is documented.
Only encryption methods (algorithms, protocols) that have been verified and certified by recognized standards bodies are used for data-at-rest protection.
Stored data (data at rest) is encrypted in accordance with the documented encryption policy.
Hard disks and storage volumes on devices, equipment, and servers are encrypted (e.g., BitLocker, hardware-based full-disk encryption).
Data stored on external storage media (USB drives, portable disks) is encrypted before or at the time of storage.
Backup data is encrypted at rest using approved methods.
Stored authentication information (passwords, tokens) is hashed and salted using approved cryptographic techniques; plaintext storage is prohibited.
Information Rights Management (IRM) or Digital Rights Management (DRM) is implemented where necessary to encrypt files, restrict reading and writing, and record operation history.
Data Loss Prevention (DLP) controls are implemented where necessary to detect and restrict data when it is moved outside the organization's control range.
Encryption algorithms in use for data at rest are regularly reviewed against published vulnerability disclosures and compromise reports; compromised algorithms are retired on a documented schedule.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Documented encryption-at-rest policy and inventory of encrypted storage assets.
BitLocker or equivalent encryption compliance reports for endpoints and servers.
DLP and IRM/DRM deployment status reports.
Results of the most recent encryption algorithm review.

controls.title: Acquiring and Protecting Backups
controls.overview: This standard establishes MCNA's requirements for acquiring, protecting, and testing backups of critical data. It ensures that backup processes are defined, backup data is stored securely and off-site, and restore procedures are regularly validated so that data can be recovered following loss, corruption, or a ransomware incident.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Permanent loss of business-critical data following a ransomware attack, hardware failure, or accidental deletion if backups are absent or untested. Extended downtime and business disruption if the recovery process is undefined or has never been validated. Regulatory or customer audit findings if backup and recovery practices cannot be evidenced. NOF Corp escalation if Secure SketCH self-assessment scores decline due to backup deficiencies.

clauses.clause_text: Backups of important data are acquired on a defined schedule, and the resulting backup data is protected against unauthorized access, modification, and deletion.
An inventory of important information that must be backed up — including file servers, database servers, and application data — is maintained and reviewed at least annually.
Backup data is protected using physical security, encryption, or both, in accordance with the encryption-at-rest standard (SSK-09-2).
Backup data is stored at a geographically remote location, separate from the primary site where the source system resides.
A documented process for recovering data from backups is maintained, covering roles, steps, and escalation procedures.
Backup frequency is defined based on the importance and change rate of each data set; backups are taken at least at the defined frequency.
Multiple backup versions are retained and managed to provide a range of restore points, enabling recovery to any point within the defined retention window.
Restore tests are performed periodically (at least annually) to verify that backup data is intact and that the recovery process completes successfully within acceptable time frames.
The backup and recovery process is reviewed and updated as appropriate based on restore-test results, infrastructure changes, and lessons learned from incidents.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Documented backup policy and inventory of backed-up systems.
Backup job logs showing successful completion at the defined frequency.
Off-site or geographically remote storage confirmation.
Restore-test results with completion time and data-integrity verification.

controls.title: Protecting Endpoints and Servers from Malware
controls.overview: This standard establishes MCNA's requirements for deploying and maintaining anti-malware protection on endpoints, servers, and network devices. It ensures that both signature-based and behavior-based detection methods are in place, kept current, and centrally managed to prevent, detect, and respond to malware infections.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Malware infection goes undetected because signature files are outdated and known attack patterns are not matched. Unknown or zero-day malware evades detection if behavior-based protection is absent or misconfigured. Lateral spread of malware across the network if endpoints or servers lack active protection. NOF Corp escalation if Secure SketCH self-assessment scores decline due to anti-malware gaps.

clauses.clause_text: Signature-based anti-malware software is deployed on all network devices, servers, and endpoints.
Anti-malware systems are configured to automatically scan for malware when external storage media is inserted or connected.
Detection status from signature-based scanning is monitored centrally and anomalies are escalated promptly.
Scanning software and pattern files (signature definition files) are updated regularly; updates are checked for and applied immediately upon availability.
Behavior-based anti-malware software is deployed on network devices, servers, and endpoints to detect malware that evades signature matching.
Behavior-based systems are configured to automatically scan when external storage media is inserted or connected.
Detection status from behavior-based scanning is monitored centrally and anomalies are escalated promptly.
Behavior-based scanning software and behavior profiles (behavior definitions) are updated regularly.
Anti-malware software across the environment is centrally managed; deployment status, update compliance, and detection events are reviewed regularly.
Malware detection methods and tools are reviewed periodically for effectiveness; gaps or emerging threats are addressed through updated tooling or configuration.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Central anti-malware console reports showing deployment coverage and agent health.
Signature and behavior-definition update compliance logs.
Detection event logs and escalation records.
Periodic effectiveness review documentation.

controls.title: Implementation of Endpoint Log Collection and Immediate Response to Malware Infection (e.g. EDR Product/Solution)
controls.overview: This standard establishes MCNA's requirements for endpoint detection and response (EDR) capabilities. It ensures that endpoint activity is logged at sufficient granularity, that mechanisms exist to detect and block malicious behavior in real time, and that response procedures—including automated remediation and simulation exercises—are maintained and regularly tested.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Malware infection may go undetected or spread unchecked if endpoint logging lacks sufficient granularity to trace malicious activity. Delayed incident response if no automated containment or remediation mechanisms are in place, allowing an attacker to establish persistence. Inability to conduct post-incident forensic analysis if command-line audit logs and endpoint telemetry are not collected. NOF Corp escalation if Secure SketCH self-assessment scores decline due to EDR coverage deficiencies.

clauses.clause_text: Endpoint logging is implemented at a granularity and level of detail sufficient for tracking malicious programs when a malware infection is detected. Logged actions include, at minimum: file read/write/print operations, OS registry operations, process starts, and network access.
Command-line audit logs (e.g., PowerShell, Bash) are collected for applicable devices, equipment, and machines.
Mechanisms are in place to prevent or preempt malicious operations, including unauthorized communication, unauthorized encrypted communication, and execution of malicious programs.
Automated remediation mechanisms are implemented to restore endpoints to a known-good state, such as deleting unauthorized programs and reversing unauthorized changes.
Logging status and the timeliness of malware-infection response are periodically validated through simulated exercises on representative devices.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: EDR console reports showing deployment coverage and agent health.
Sample endpoint logs demonstrating required granularity (file ops, registry, processes, network).
Automated remediation event records.
Simulation exercise results with response-time measurements.

controls.title: Network Segmentation
controls.overview: Enforce network segmentation appropriate to MCNA's organizational structure and operations so that compromise of one segment does not enable lateral movement to others, and so that access between segments is restricted to authorized, business-justified flows.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by material network or business changes as listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by material network or business changes as listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Unintended actors, or users not originally intended to have access, may reach information and systems outside their need-to-know. In an unsegmented environment, malware infection can spread across the organization via the network, reaching other devices and segments. NOF Corp escalation if Secure SketCH self-assessment scores decline due to segmentation gaps.

clauses.clause_text: Prepare a segmentation design that aligns with MCNA's organizational structure and business operations, documented in a current network architecture diagram.
Design each segment to allow only the minimum two-way communication required for its business function.
Segregate the data plane (production communication traffic) from the control plane (network management traffic).
Demarcate segments at the level of business unit, organizational unit, or department where operationally feasible.
Design segments under the assumption that a malicious actor has already gained the capability of lateral movement, including from an external compromise.
Roll out physical and logical network segmentation in accordance with the approved network architecture.
Perform network management operations from an isolated environment or device that is separate from the main production network.
Implement host-level segmentation or micro-segmentation where risk and operational management load justify it.
Ensure that only authorized systems can communicate across isolated network segments, enforced at firewalls, ACLs, or equivalent controls.
Regularly review and monitor the operating status and effectiveness of network segmentation, and adjust or improve the design as the environment, threat landscape, or business changes.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current network architecture diagram showing segments, trust boundaries, and approved flows.
Firewall and ACL rule sets demonstrating enforcement of segmentation.
Records of segmentation reviews, including findings and remediation.

controls.title: Denying Communication Which Is Not Permitted
controls.overview: Block connections from unauthorized IP addresses or ports to internal and external networks, so that only expressly authorized communication is permitted, and so that the definitions of unauthorized communication are kept current.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with rule-level changes managed continuously and out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with rule-level changes managed continuously and out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Internal systems may be exposed to threats from the public internet and to malicious access from compromised hosts. Lateral movement and data exfiltration if unauthorized communication paths between VLANs or segments are not blocked. Drift from the approved baseline may go undetected if configuration comparison and alerting are not implemented. NOF Corp escalation if Secure SketCH self-assessment scores decline due to firewall or communication-control gaps.

clauses.clause_text: Block communication over unauthorized IP addresses or ports at perimeter and internal enforcement points.
Define and restrict disallowed communication after segmentation has been implemented, using on-premises or cloud-native enforcement.
Deny traffic over disallowed or blocked TCP and UDP ports.
Between VLANs, allow only authorized systems to communicate, and only with other systems specifically identified for that purpose.
Implement and manage virtual firewalls and OS-level firewalls on servers.
Use a whitelist (allowlist) approach for firewall settings, in which only expressly allowed and necessary communication is permitted.
When a blocklist method is used in addition to allowlists, collect threat information as appropriate and add it to the rules.
Ensure unauthorized communications are properly restricted by validating rule effectiveness on a defined cadence.
Regularly scan devices deployed in the network, including hardware firewalls, using vulnerability scanners.
Implement mechanisms to compare network equipment settings against an approved baseline and to receive (and not miss) notifications when a deviation is detected.
Record network packets that cross the boundary, sufficient to support post-incident investigation.
Regularly review the definition of communication to be rejected and update rules accordingly.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Firewall and ACL rule sets, including allowlist documentation.
Configuration baseline comparison reports and deviation alerts.
Boundary packet capture or flow log retention records.
Records of periodic rule reviews.

controls.category_name: Network Monitoring and Web Security Standards
controls.title: Detection of Unauthorized Communication from Outside
controls.overview: Detect unauthorized communication originating from outside the organization, block it where appropriate, and review detection trends to keep definitions and responses current.
controls.cadence: Policies reviewed quarterly; trend analysis reviewed annually.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Policies reviewed quarterly; trend analysis reviewed annually.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Unauthorized communication from outside the organization cannot be detected or blocked, allowing improper access to internal resources. In the event of malware infection, communication with command-and-control (C&C) servers may go undetected, allowing attackers to maintain control of compromised hosts.

clauses.clause_text: Detect unauthorized communications from outside the organization at the network perimeter.
Implement IDS and IPS, and customize their policy settings to MCNA's environment and traffic profile.
Monitor the internal network and detect unusual or suspicious traffic, including by use of NDR or equivalent capabilities.
Inspect the content of communication suspected or proven to be unauthorized or improper, and block or contain it where necessary.
Review the definition of unauthorized communication and the response to it on a defined cadence, informed by detection trend analysis.
Regularly review IDS and IPS policy settings and adjust them based on operational experience and emerging threats.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: IDS, IPS, and NDR deployment records and policy configurations.
Detection trend analyses and rule tuning records.
Records of containment or block actions taken in response to detections.

controls.category_name: Network Monitoring and Web Security Standards
controls.title: Logging Internet Access and Activity
controls.overview: Aggregate internet connections and routing so that all internet access is fully logged, and ensure periodic audit of communication content to support detection and incident response.
controls.cadence: Configuration reviewed annually; audit sampling on a defined quarterly cycle.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Configuration reviewed annually; audit sampling on a defined quarterly cycle.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Access to the internet is not logged. In the event of an infection or other cyber incident, users and source devices cannot be reliably identified.

clauses.clause_text: Obtain internet access logs from all egress points used by MCNA users and systems.
Use proxy servers or Secure Web Gateways (SWG) to obtain logs of all internet access, including URL requests and DNS queries.
When proxy servers or SWGs are introduced, restrict internet access that does not pass through the aggregation route.
Regularly audit the contents of internet access communication for indicators of unauthorized use, data exfiltration, or compromise.
Decrypt SSL/TLS traffic at controlled inspection points and monitor its content where legally and operationally permitted.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Proxy and SWG configuration records.
Log retention configuration and storage records.
Records of periodic content audits and findings.
Documentation of SSL/TLS inspection scope and exclusions.

controls.category_name: Network Monitoring and Web Security Standards
controls.title: Web Access Restriction (Implementation of Web Content Filtering)
controls.overview: Define and restrict the websites and web categories to which access is permitted or denied, and review allow and deny lists on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Reviewed semi-annually; ad hoc updates as risk warrants.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Reviewed semi-annually; ad hoc updates as risk warrants.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Sensitive information may leak to internet services such as cloud storage, social media, public bulletin boards, and web mail. Malware infection may occur due to access to a malicious site loaded with malware. In the event of malware infection, command-and-control (C&C) communication may not be blocked, allowing attackers to maintain control of compromised hosts.

clauses.clause_text: Define websites and categories to which access is expressly permitted or expressly denied.
Maintain a blocklist that includes sites and categories not necessary for business purposes, including internet storage services where they are not approved.
Use DNS filtering services to blocklist access to known malicious domains.
Use allowlists for sites and categories that are required for business purposes.
Restrict access to websites by use of web filtering capabilities deployed on endpoints, on the network, or both.
Periodically review websites and categories to which access is permitted or denied, and adjust based on business need and threat landscape.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Allow and block list documentation, including business justification.
Web filtering and DNS filtering configuration records.
Records of periodic list reviews and changes.

controls.category_name: Network Monitoring and Web Security Standards
controls.title: Attack Detection and Response to Web Applications (Implementation of WAF, etc.)
controls.overview: Detect and protect against attacks on web applications from external networks, including by use of a Web Application Firewall (WAF) or equivalent capability, and review detection conditions on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Policies reviewed quarterly; incident review as events occur.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Policies reviewed quarterly; incident review as events occur.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Attacks on important web applications cannot be detected and prevented, including credential stuffing and exploitation of application-layer vulnerabilities.

clauses.clause_text: Detect external attacks and intrusions to web applications using a WAF or equivalent capability.
Inspect all traffic passing through to in-scope web applications.
Where traffic is encrypted, perform inspection after SSL termination on an enabled device or after authorized decryption.
Where it is operationally difficult to change the network configuration, use a hosted Web Application Firewall.
Defend against external attacks and intrusions to detected web applications by enforcing block, challenge, or rate-limit actions.
Regularly review filtering and detection policies for web applications, and review detected anomalies and suspected or proven incidents.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: WAF deployment and policy configuration records.
Inspection records, including SSL termination configuration.
Detection logs and incident review records.

controls.title: Response to Abnormal Increase in Traffic
controls.overview: Establish a policy for detecting and responding to abnormal increases in communication traffic, including denial-of-service conditions, so that service disruption is minimized and response is timely.
controls.cadence: Reviewed annually; baselines refreshed semi-annually.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Reviewed annually; baselines refreshed semi-annually.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Higher traffic levels may go undetected, resulting in network or service suspension. A DDoS attack may not be detected, and the response could be delayed or lead to system or service suspension.

clauses.clause_text: Monitor and understand normal traffic volumes for in-scope services.
Establish normal load levels and traffic volumes as a benchmark, and configure alerts when thresholds are exceeded.
Formulate the response to be followed when traffic exceeding the threshold is detected.
Audit all external-facing servers (public-facing servers) and conduct an impact assessment to understand the impact of disruption.
Implement a DDoS countermeasure (such as a service or solution) at the network boundary for services whose outage or degradation would have material business impact.
Create procedures and define the response flow when a DDoS attack occurs, including roles, escalation, and recovery steps.
Regularly check detected issues and implement measures to ensure stable operation, including expansion of network capacity where warranted.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Traffic baselines and threshold configuration records.
DDoS countermeasure deployment records.
Documented response procedures and tabletop or live-event records.

controls.title: Establishing and Disseminating Usage Rules for Remote Access
controls.overview: Define and disseminate the rules under which users are allowed remote access to MCNA systems, including permitted users, purposes, environments, and required security measures, so that remote access is granted intentionally and reviewed on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Reviewed annually and on material change.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Reviewed annually and on material change.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: An unplanned approach to remote access security may lead to a reactive — and therefore inconsistent and incomplete — response to cyber threats.

clauses.clause_text: Define usage rules for remote access, including permitted users, business purposes, permitted environments, and required security measures.
Communicate the remote access usage rules to users and provide approved access environments as needed.
Minimize the remote access environment provided by MCNA to what is required for business purposes.
Regularly review permitted users and required security measures for remote access, and adjust as the user population and threat landscape change.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Remote access usage rules document, with version history.
Records of communication of rules to users.
Remote access user inventory and review records.

controls.title: Control of Remote Access
controls.overview: Introduce technical measures that enable remote access to be used safely, including encryption of communication, authentication of users and devices, posture checks, session management, and ongoing monitoring.
controls.cadence: Configuration reviewed annually; usage monitored continuously.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Configuration reviewed annually; usage monitored continuously.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Information leakage may occur due to eavesdropping or interception of remote access communication. Unauthorized devices, including personal devices that do not meet MCNA security requirements and third-party devices, may connect to MCNA systems. Remote access authentication may be permitted using spoofed or stolen credentials, allowing unauthorized parties to act as legitimate users.

clauses.clause_text: Define and implement technical measures for secure remote access aligned to the remote access usage rules.
Implement access control solutions such as VPN or Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) to encrypt communication that connects to internal systems.
Implement device authentication mechanisms, such as client certificate authentication, in addition to user authentication.
In addition to ID and password authentication, implement an additional authentication factor (multi-factor authentication) appropriate to business and user authority levels.
Restrict remote access from devices that have not completed required posture or hardening settings.
Lock a remote terminal when the number of authentication failures exceeds a defined threshold.
Terminate the network connection at the end of a session or after a period of inactivity.
Use Mobile Device Management (MDM) on mobile devices to allow remote wipe in the event of loss or theft.
Where personally owned devices are permitted for full or partial business use, separate the business workspace from personal data on the device.
Verify that remote access is being used securely, including in accordance with the rules in SSK-12-1.
Monitor remote access usage to ensure that only authorized users and devices are establishing remote connections.
Where the internet is directly accessible from a remote terminal, obtain access logs on that terminal.
Regularly review the measures for safe use of remote access and update them based on operational experience and threat landscape.
Periodically rotate hardware tokens and certificates, replacing them with new credentials on a defined cadence.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: VPN/ZTNA configuration records and certificate inventory.
MFA enrollment and authentication logs.
MDM policy configuration and enrolled-device inventory.
Remote access monitoring records and exception logs.

controls.title: Wireless Communication Management
controls.overview: Establish a policy for wireless communication usage, manage devices that perform wireless communication, encrypt wireless communication, and review the policy and safeguards on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Reviewed annually and on material change.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Reviewed annually and on material change.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Eavesdropping or interception of wireless communication may be possible, leading to information leakage. Wireless authentication may be permitted using spoofed or stolen credentials, allowing unauthorized parties to access MCNA systems.

clauses.clause_text: Establish a wireless communication usage policy, including rules for use of public wireless LAN (public Wi-Fi) during remote work.
Implement protective measures for wireless communication based on the wireless communication usage policy.
Disable wireless communication on devices when there is no business need for it.
Restrict device access to permitted wireless networks where there is a business need.
Use secure cryptographic algorithms and current authentication protocols for wireless communication, including 802.1X and current Wi-Fi security standards.
Regularly review the wireless communication usage policy and the measures used for safe wireless communication.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Wireless communication usage policy with version history.
Wireless network configuration records, including encryption and authentication standards.
Records of policy reviews and updates.

controls.title: Management of Wireless Access Points
controls.overview: This standard establishes requirements for managing wireless access points permitted to connect to the MCNA network, detecting unauthorized access points, and reviewing installation and management practices on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Inventory reviewed quarterly; methodology and detection rules reviewed at least annually.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Inventory reviewed quarterly; methodology and detection rules reviewed at least annually.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Connections to unauthorized access points may enable eavesdropping and interception of internal communication, information leakage, and credential compromise. Without continuous detection, rogue access points may persist undetected and provide a foothold for lateral movement into MCNA systems.

clauses.clause_text: Maintain an inventory of wireless access points authorized to connect to the MCNA network, using a list, database, or ledger.
Restrict access to corporate networks where wireless access points are provided to devices outside MCNA control, including personal devices and guest devices.
Detect when an unauthorized wireless access point is connected to the network and take corrective action, including removal.
Deploy wireless intrusion detection or prevention systems (WIDS/WIPS) to automatically detect and respond to unauthorized wireless access points.
Periodically review wireless access point installation and management methods, and adjust based on operational experience and threat landscape.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Authorized access point inventory.
WIDS/WIPS deployment and detection records.
Records of unauthorized access point detections and remediation actions.

controls.title: Security Check on Incoming Mail
controls.overview: This standard establishes requirements for spam filtering, attachment malware scanning, URL inspection, and sender authentication on incoming email, and for reviewing inbound security checkpoints on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Configuration reviewed quarterly; trend analysis at least annually.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Configuration reviewed quarterly; trend analysis at least annually.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Incoming email with malware attachments may be delivered to MCNA users, and infection from such email may not be prevented. Incoming email with executable or other high-risk attachments commonly used to distribute malware (such as .bat, .exe, .vbs, .lnk) may not be blocked. Without the ability to verify URL safety in email bodies, MCNA users may follow malicious links. Malware-attached email may reach users before pattern files (malware definitions or spam registries) are updated, leading to infection.

clauses.clause_text: Define security guidance for incoming email, including filtering, scanning, and acceptance criteria.
Based on the defined guidance, check incoming email and restrict delivery as necessary.
Implement email filtering solutions and services that perform virus scans on attached files.
Block received email with attachments that include high-risk file extensions (such as .bat, .exe, .vbs, .lnk) where they are not required for business purposes.
Implement filtering solutions and services to filter spam email.
Verify SPF, DKIM, and DMARC policies on inbound mail and act on authentication results.
Implement a mechanism to temporarily hold email containing attachments or URLs to allow sufficient time for virus scans and definition updates.
Analyze and block email attachments and URLs using sandbox features where available.
Regularly review the security guidance for incoming email and the implementation measures used.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Inbound email filtering and scanning configuration records.
SPF, DKIM, and DMARC verification settings and reports.
Sandboxing and URL rewriting deployment records.
Records of periodic configuration reviews.

controls.title: Enabling Security of Outbound Email Communication
controls.overview: This standard establishes requirements to prevent misdelivery of outbound email, prevent unauthorized sending, prevent spoofing of MCNA domains, and review the outbound email security release flow on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Configuration reviewed at least annually; sender authentication monitored continuously.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Configuration reviewed at least annually; sender authentication monitored continuously.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Outgoing email, if not subject to release controls, may be sent to incorrect recipients and disclose confidential information. Preventive controls against internal wrongdoing via email may be ineffective without supervisor approval and content controls. Without sender domain authentication, MCNA domains may be spoofed in phishing campaigns targeting customers or partners.

clauses.clause_text: Define and implement measures to prevent misdelivered email (including delivery to incorrect recipients), unauthorized sending, and spoofing.
Implement email security features at the time of sending, based on the defined measures.
Restrict or block outgoing email as necessary, based on policy and risk.
Implement email filtering solutions or services to restrict or prevent autocompletion of recipient addresses (To: fields) for sensitive recipient classes.
Encrypt email attachments when sent to external recipients, and require supervisor approval where the policy requires it.
Use a dedicated approved file sharing service to share files externally, in lieu of email attachments where appropriate.
