Configure sender domain authentication, including SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, for MCNA-controlled domains.
Regularly review security measures governing outbound email, and implement new technology or update existing measures based on operational experience and threat landscape.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Outbound email control configuration records.
SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records for MCNA domains.
Approved external file sharing service configuration.
Records of periodic outbound email reviews.

controls.title: Establishing and Communicating Policies or Rules Addressing Use of Cloud Services
controls.overview: This standard establishes requirements for defining and communicating rules governing the use of cloud services to all users, stakeholders, and concerned parties, and for reviewing those rules on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Policy and approved cloud services list reviewed at least annually; provider evaluations performed at onboarding and on material change.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Policy and approved cloud services list reviewed at least annually; provider evaluations performed at onboarding and on material change.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Use of cloud operator services that do not follow appropriate security requirements may cause system suspensions and outages or lead to information leakage. Without defined selection criteria and review, unsanctioned cloud adoption may bypass MCNA security and contractual safeguards. Failure to communicate cloud usage rules may result in users storing or processing data in inappropriate services or jurisdictions.

clauses.clause_text: Define policies and rules for safe use of cloud services.
Define which cloud operators and services are permitted, or establish selection criteria.
Confirm there is no discrepancy between the service provider's and MCNA's security policies.
Confirm that security measures required by MCNA are implemented, and that risk assessment is performed regularly.

When data is stored on a cloud service, confirm that data ownership and intellectual property rights belong to MCNA, and that the geographic location of the data center is appropriate (including with respect to offshore replication).
Confirm that agreements such as SLA, disclaimers for liability, damages and assurances for liability, and conditions for termination of service agreement are in place and enforced or enforceable.
Classify service providers according to the confidentiality and volume of data handled on cloud services, and identify and select requirements according to the classification.
Document security measures and other considerations that should be implemented or followed by cloud service users, and notify the users of this document.
Define the information that is allowed to be stored in a cloud service and label it according to its data classification.
Understand all security risks that could materialize because of the use of cloud services.
Appoint a person in charge (point of contact) for service management, and establish responsibility for management of security for cloud services.
Maintain contact information of cloud service providers and MCNA stakeholder parties (RACI), and establish an organizational system that can respond quickly in an incident.
Formally notify policies and rules to cloud service users.
Regularly review the contents of policies and rules.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Cloud services usage policy with version history.
Approved cloud services list and selection criteria documentation.
Records of provider evaluations and risk assessments.
Records of communications of policies to users.

controls.title: Development of Processes for the Use of Cloud Services
controls.overview: Establish a workflow for the use of cloud services — including approval, inventory, change, and end-of-use — and review the workflow on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Reviewed annually and on material change.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Reviewed annually and on material change.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Using cloud operator services that do not follow appropriate security requirements can cause system suspensions and outages, or data leaks.

clauses.clause_text: Develop a process for using cloud services.
Establish a process to require prior request before using a cloud service, and the approving or management authority must check the request against the selection criteria.
Manage all cloud services in use in a list or ledger, including the intended use and supervising or owning departments.
When ending the use of a cloud service, follow a process to request approval for end-of-use, confirm whether stored data is properly discarded, and update the list or ledger.
When updating the contract or service for a cloud service, conduct a risk assessment for continued use.
Manage cloud services in accordance with the prescribed processes.
Regularly review this process.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Cloud service request and approval workflow records.
Cloud services inventory or ledger.
End-of-use approval and data disposal records.
Records of process reviews.

controls.title: Security Settings for Cloud Services
controls.overview: Set appropriate configuration settings for cloud services on the user’s side, having established a clear understanding of security and administration responsibilities, and verify these settings on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Configuration reviewed quarterly; CSPM/SSPM monitored continuously.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Configuration reviewed quarterly; CSPM/SSPM monitored continuously.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Improper or unsafe settings may result in unintended information being made public, or access keys being disclosed.

clauses.clause_text: Implement cloud service security settings that can be set by the service user.
Use the recommended settings provided by the cloud service provider, or applicable industry standard or industry recommended settings.
Identify and implement measures from guidelines that explain common configuration mistakes often made by both service providers and users.
Review security settings as necessary according to changes in how the service is used, including changes in the data handled (stored, processed, etc.).
Implement security administration settings comprehensively after understanding responsibilities around use (terms of use, etc.) on the part of cloud service users.
Regularly confirm that network communication with cloud services, and the data and resources stored on cloud services, are properly protected.
Continuously assess configuration and settings of cloud services using tools such as Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) and SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM).

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Cloud service configuration baselines.
CSPM/SSPM deployment and findings records.
Records of periodic configuration verifications.
Evidence of remediation of misconfigurations.

controls.title: Visualization and Control of Cloud Services Usage
controls.overview: Inspect access to cloud services, understand the usage situation, and control the use of unauthorized services.
controls.cadence: Reviewed quarterly; usage monitored continuously.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Reviewed quarterly; usage monitored continuously.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Insufficient oversight on the use of unauthorized cloud services (shadow IT) may result in improper use without the organization’s knowledge. Insufficient oversight on the content of communication to cloud services may result in spread of malware infections or information leakage.

clauses.clause_text: Monitor communication contents and detect unauthorized or disallowed use of cloud services that are not permitted.
Prevent use of unauthorized or disallowed cloud services using technology systems (software, hardware, etc.).
Use Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) or similar tools (e.g., SSL/TLS decryption) to monitor data uploads to cloud services, and set controls to trigger based on flagged content.
Regularly review approved and disallowed cloud services to ensure that usage is controlled.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: CASB/cloud monitoring deployment records.
Detection and prevention configuration records.
Shadow IT discovery reports.
Records of periodic reviews of approved and disallowed services.

controls.title: Enabling Logging of Systems and Acquired Logs
controls.overview: Acquire logs after determining the targets and methods, and review the targets and methods on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Reviewed annually; log acquisition monitored continuously.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Reviewed annually; log acquisition monitored continuously.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Log entries may be incomplete, or items subject to logging may be missed, resulting in delays in detection of incidents. Insufficient or deficient logs may hamper analysis, resulting in inability to conduct root cause analysis or assess impact after an incident.

clauses.clause_text: Identify and define systems subject to logging, the location and period of log storage, and obtain those logs.
Enable audit logging to acquire detailed information including event source, date, user, timestamp, source address, destination address, and other useful fields.
Obtain all access logs, including updates and deletions, to sensitive data.
Synchronize the time sources across servers and network devices to ensure timestamps in logs are consistent.
Use at least two synchronized time sources across corporate assets.
Where relevant laws and regulations such as privacy protection apply, log information in compliance with those requirements.
Log authentication and authorization events, data creation, update, and deletion events, and user management events for each system service.
Regularly confirm that logs are acquired to meet defined requirements.
Raise alerts when logging stops or experiences another failure event.
Periodically review items and assets subject to log acquisition and the methods for log acquisition.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Log acquisition target list and configuration records.
Time synchronization configuration records.
Logging failure alert configuration.
Records of periodic reviews of log scope and methods.

controls.title: Storing, Retaining, and Protecting Logs
controls.overview: Store logs for the required period and protect them from unauthorized access, and verify protection on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Reviewed annually; access reviewed quarterly.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Reviewed annually; access reviewed quarterly.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Logs may be open to tampering, deletion, or disabling during cyberattacks, hampering or disabling forensics and root-cause investigations.

clauses.clause_text: Confirm that the storage period of acquired logs meets national laws and industry regulations; in general, retain logs for at least 12 months.
Verify that the log storage location has sufficient storage space.
Retain logs for an appropriately set number of past iterations (define and store a configured number of iterations over the log's history).
Store logs in a location outside the system from which they were obtained, and at a remote, geographically separated location, to protect logs from tampering or unauthorized access.
Restrict access to logs to the fewest number of users needed.
Encrypt logs as needed, based on a judgment of the importance of the information they contain.
Regularly verify that logs are protected appropriately and that there is no fraudulent access.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Log storage and retention configuration records.
Log access control configuration and access reviews.
Log encryption configuration where applicable.
Records of periodic protection verifications.

controls.title: Enabling Analysis of Acquired Systems Logs
controls.overview: When suspicious behavior is identified through log analysis, respond first by notifying the responsible person, and review analysis techniques and response methods on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Procedures reviewed annually; rules tuned continuously based on incidents and threat intelligence.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Procedures reviewed annually; rules tuned continuously based on incidents and threat intelligence.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Detection of cyberattacks may be delayed or impossible, delaying first response or other initial response measures.

clauses.clause_text: Analyze acquired logs and detect security events.
Identify and centrally manage logs necessary for detecting signs of an incident.
Define the mechanism for detecting signs of an incident, log analysis procedures, and notification flow.
Periodically analyze logs and specify incident warning thresholds for automatic detection, in accordance with predetermined processes.
Determine monitoring items and monitoring time (24 hours / 365 days, business hours only, etc.) according to business needs.
When analyzing logs, eliminate irrelevant logs and extract meaningful logs to streamline analysis instead of targeting all logs.
Notify the appropriate personnel quickly when an incident is suspected.
Establish a Security Operations Center (SOC) that handles 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
Analyze logs to estimate the impact and scope of detected events.
Regularly review log analysis methods, viewpoints, and response methods.
Review the analytical perspective of logs based on threat intelligence.
Test the defined detection process for effectiveness and periodically review it for improvement after operation starts.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Log analysis procedures and detection rule documentation.
SOC operations records and notification logs.
Detection effectiveness test records.
Records of analysis review and threat-intelligence-driven tuning.

controls.title: Enabling Log Correlation and Analyzing Logs Across Sources
controls.overview: Collect logs and data from multiple sources, analyze and visualize the correlations between them, and review correlation analysis methods on a defined cadence.
controls.cadence: Reviewed annually; rule tuning continuous.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with DIS Computers (MSP) as implementer.
controls.status_description: Reviewed annually; rule tuning continuous.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Logs or traces of incident activity may not be detected when looking at logs in isolation, in the absence of a comprehensive cross-source correlation approach.

clauses.clause_text: Detect security events by correlating and analyzing multiple logs.
Perform real-time analysis to detect correlation among logs using tools such as SIEM.
Correlate and analyze multiple logs to notify and respond to detected events in a manner appropriate to the specifics of the logs.
Periodically review logs, data, and methods for correlation analysis.
Regularly tune the settings of log correlation analysis systems, such as SIEM, to improve the accuracy of correlation analysis.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: SIEM deployment and rule configuration records.
Correlation rule tuning records.
Cross-source detection records and incident review notes.
Records of periodic correlation analysis reviews.

controls.title: Establishing and Communicating Policies or Rules for the System Development Lifecycle
controls.overview: This standard defines the rules and practices that govern how MCNA designs, builds, installs, operates, and changes information systems. It establishes the policy framework that ensures security is considered consistently across every stage of the system development lifecycle (SDLC), rather than addressed reactively after deployment.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: SDLC activities may proceed without consistent security requirements, producing systems with avoidable vulnerabilities that surface only after deployment. External partners and internal staff may apply inconsistent standards, creating gaps that audit, penetration test, or incident review later attribute to undefined rules. Changes may reach production without documented review and approval, increasing the likelihood of outages, data exposure, or non-compliance findings.

clauses.clause_text: Rules and practices governing software development are defined and incorporate information-security considerations across the lifecycle (planning, design, implementation, testing, release, operation, retirement).
Rules for system design are defined and require explicit consideration of confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements proportionate to the sensitivity and criticality of the system.
Rules to classify data and to enact protective measures based on identified sensitivity are defined, aligned with MCNA data classification standards.
Rules to grant only minimum-necessary privileges and to restrict unnecessary access are defined and applied to development, test, and production environments.
Rules addressing the use of cloud services are defined, aligned with MCNA Standard SSK-15 (Cloud Services), and applied to all SDLC activities involving SaaS, PaaS, or IaaS.
Rules governing system implementation and rollout are defined, including criteria for staged release, rollback, and post-release verification.
Secure coding guidelines are defined, kept current with industry references (e.g., OWASP), and made available to anyone writing or reviewing code on MCNA's behalf.
Rules addressing the use of external components — open-source libraries, third-party packages, and vendor SDKs — are defined and require evaluation before adoption.
Rules addressing the operation and running of systems are defined, including hardening baselines, change-management requirements, and operational monitoring.
Rules addressing the acquisition of necessary logs are defined, aligned with MCNA Standard SSK-16 (Logging).
Rules for vulnerability management and periodic security assessments and audits are defined, aligned with MCNA Standard SSK-07 (Vulnerability Management).
Change-management rules addressing modifications and changes to systems are defined; no change reaches production without documented review and approval per the rule set.
Established rules are communicated to responsible individuals — internal staff, DIS Computers personnel, and other vendors — at onboarding and on material change, with acknowledgement recorded.

Established and defined rules are reviewed at least annually, and additionally when triggered by the events listed in Section 6, by the IT-MIS Director with input from DIS Computers and System Owners.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current SDLC rule set with revision history.
Acknowledgement records from responsible internal staff and external partners.
Most recent annual review minutes signed by the IT-MIS Director and CFO.
Cross-references to MCNA Standards SSK-07, SSK-15, and SSK-16.

controls.title: Security-Conscious System Design
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA designs information systems with security treated as a primary design constraint, not a late-stage adjustment. It establishes the planning, principles, and review activities required before a system advances past the design stage.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Security flaws baked into system architectures that are expensive or impossible to remediate post-deployment. Audit findings citing missing or stale architecture diagrams and design-stage security reviews. Incidents and outages from systems lacking documented redundancy, load balancing, or monitoring metrics. Regulatory exposure where designs cannot demonstrate adherence to NOF Corporate guidance or contractual obligations.

clauses.clause_text: For each functional and non-functional requirement of the system, the security viewpoints to be checked at the design stage are understood and formalized according to risk and business importance.
Beginning at the planning phase of the development lifecycle, the system's objectives and the information assets to be protected are understood, and risk-response strategies are established.
A baseline configuration is established in accordance with system design principles, including the principle of developing only the essential functionality required.
Secure-design principles are enforced, including the principle of least privilege (PoLP), separation of duties, defense in depth, and validation of all user input.
For each system, the business impact of downtime in the event of failure is evaluated, and load balancing and redundancy are implemented to meet the acceptable downtime.
Confidential information stored in reusable resources — memory, disk, caches — is erased immediately when no longer needed.
Metrics to be monitored (e.g., CPU, memory, throughput, error rate) are identified at design time, and appropriate alerts are configured before deployment.
Systems are designed with explicit consideration of information security, following the viewpoints and methodology identified during the planning stage.

Security reviews are conducted at the system design stage; instructions for improvements — including refinement of the design or alternatives that meet security requirements — are issued where design gaps are identified.
When improvements are issued under clause 17-2.9, implementation is reassessed and confirmed before the system advances past the design stage.
System architecture diagrams are created to visualize communication and data flows for every system in scope.
Information-security and cybersecurity aspects of system designs are reviewed at least annually.
System architecture diagrams are updated whenever a material change is made and reviewed at least annually.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current set of system architecture diagrams with revision dates.
Design-stage security review records and improvement instructions.
Risk-response strategies documented for in-scope systems.
Records of baseline configuration definitions and least-privilege design decisions.

controls.title: Security-Conscious System Installation
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA implements and tests information systems with security in mind, covering the configuration, source-code, environment-isolation, and CI/CD controls required from the start of implementation through to release.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Insecure code, defaults, or third-party components reaching production without identification or remediation. Audit findings citing missing secure-coding acknowledgements, absent SAST/DAST evidence, or unrestricted CI/CD access. Data exposure from using unmasked production data in non-production environments. Operational incidents traceable to lack of environment isolation or release-stage controls.

clauses.clause_text: Cybersecurity considerations to be checked at the implementation and testing phases are understood and formalized prior to start of implementation.
Unneeded configurations or settings in infrastructure or source code are removed or disabled, applying the principle of least privilege.
Developers — internal staff and external partners — are educated on MCNA's secure-coding guidelines and are required to acknowledge them prior to contributing code.
Access to infrastructure and source code is restricted to authorized personnel; standing access is replaced with role-based and time-bound access where feasible.
Only latest, reliable external components are used in development, following due approval by a designated specialist team and verification that the component is actively maintained.
Code signing or equivalent integrity techniques are used to detect unauthorized changes to external components and internally produced artifacts.
Functions to validate user input — covering data size, type, format, and allowable values — are implemented for all externally exposed interfaces.

When systems share a common platform with other tenants (multitenant cloud platforms, shared servers), MCNA data is protected from access by other tenants or their processes through tenant isolation controls.
CI/CD pipelines are built to prevent release mistakes and unwanted changes, including automated checks, peer review gates, and reproducible build outputs.
Systems are implemented and tested in line with the cybersecurity considerations formalized under clause 17-3.1.
Production, staging, development, and test environments are physically or virtually isolated from one another according to the required security level.
Test data is created and selected to meet test requirements; representativeness is balanced against the obligation to protect confidential information.

Production data is not used as test data as a default. Where production data must be used, confidential fields are hidden using techniques such as data masking, tokenization, or deterministic obfuscation.
Static and dynamic application security testing tools (SAST and DAST) are used to verify adherence to secure-coding guidelines before release.
Security considerations applied during implementation and testing are reviewed at least annually and on material change to the development toolchain.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Secure-coding guideline acknowledgements for developers and partners.
CI/CD pipeline configuration and access-control records.
Most recent SAST and DAST scan reports and remediation tracking.
Records of test-data masking decisions for any production-data use.

controls.title: Security-Conscious System Operation
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA operates and maintains information systems with security in mind, covering administrator access, change management, encryption-key handling, configuration management, and continuous monitoring obligations.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Unauthorized administrative actions and lateral movement enabled by missing MFA, weak credentials, or shared admin devices. Audit findings citing unsupported software in production without compensating controls or documented exceptions. Cryptographic compromise from poorly managed encryption keys. Service disruption from unmanaged change, unmonitored availability thresholds, or undocumented operational baselines.

clauses.clause_text: Cybersecurity considerations to be checked at the operation and maintenance phases are understood and formalized as MCNA operational standards.
A dedicated device or system is used for important administrative work and is separated from devices used for general computing.
The impact on other systems is tested before any change to system configuration or settings is applied to production.
The security impact of changes is analyzed and documented before any change to system configuration or settings is applied.
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for any maintenance performed by remote access from an external network.
Version support is verified for all software acquired from outside the organization; software past end of vendor support is identified and tracked.

Where unsupported (end-of-life) software must be used for an unavoidable business reason, risks are identified, additional measures (such as network isolation) are implemented, and renewal and replacement plans are documented.
The interface between administrator functions and normal user functions is physically or logically separated.
Export of confidential information from MCNA systems is restricted using technology-based controls, and explicit approval is required whenever such export is needed.

clauses.group_name: Configuration, Key Management, and Continuous Monitoring
clauses.clause_text: Systems are operated and maintained according to the formalized security considerations in clause 17-4.1.

clauses.group_name: Configuration, Key Management, and Continuous Monitoring
clauses.clause_text: When operation is outsourced, MCNA confirms that the outsourced operator is operating and maintaining the system in line with this standard, with evidence reviewed at least annually.

clauses.group_name: Configuration, Key Management, and Continuous Monitoring
clauses.clause_text: Tools, methods, and personnel used to perform system maintenance are managed, with each privileged action tied to an approved change record or maintenance ticket.

clauses.group_name: Configuration, Key Management, and Continuous Monitoring
clauses.clause_text: Encryption keys used in systems are managed securely throughout their lifecycle: generation, distribution, storage, rotation, and destruction.

clauses.group_name: Configuration, Key Management, and Continuous Monitoring
clauses.clause_text: System configuration is managed using infrastructure-as-code (IaC) where feasible, with version-controlled definitions and reproducible deployments.

clauses.group_name: Configuration, Key Management, and Continuous Monitoring
clauses.clause_text: Secure protocols (e.g., SSH, HTTPS, TLS-protected RDP) are used to access administrative interfaces; legacy protocols are disabled.

clauses.group_name: Configuration, Key Management, and Continuous Monitoring
clauses.clause_text: Default accounts on devices and services used in systems are disabled or have their credentials changed prior to production use.

clauses.group_name: Configuration, Key Management, and Continuous Monitoring
clauses.clause_text: Software bills of materials (SBOMs) are created and managed for systems where feasible, and used to support vulnerability response.

clauses.group_name: Configuration, Key Management, and Continuous Monitoring
clauses.clause_text: Security considerations applied during operation and maintenance are reviewed at least annually and on material change to the operating environment.

clauses.group_name: Configuration, Key Management, and Continuous Monitoring
clauses.clause_text: Availability (uptime) of system resources — servers, storage, networks — is monitored against defined thresholds, with alerting on degradation.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Most recent operational standards review minutes.
Records of MFA enforcement on remote maintenance and SSH/HTTPS for admin interfaces.
EoL software inventory with documented exceptions and additional controls.
Outsourced operation conformance records and IaC repository access logs.

controls.title: Conducting Vulnerability Scans
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA discovers and addresses vulnerabilities through a combination of scanning mechanisms, code review, and triggered scans, ensuring that systems are continuously evaluated against known and emerging threats.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Critical vulnerabilities reaching or remaining in production undetected. Audit findings citing missing scan coverage across SAST, DAST, SCA, network, cloud, or container categories. Incident-response delays where exposure to a disclosed CVE cannot be quickly determined. Regulatory and contractual exposure where vulnerability-management evidence cannot be produced on request.

clauses.clause_text: At least one scan is performed using scanning tools to check for vulnerabilities in systems, infrastructure, or applications, and response or remediation is executed for findings as required.
A dedicated account, IP address, and machine are used for vulnerability scanning to allow scan traffic to be distinguished from legitimate traffic and to limit blast radius.
Source code is checked for vulnerabilities using static application security testing (SAST) or equivalent means.
Web applications are checked for vulnerabilities using dynamic application security testing (DAST), web application scanners, or equivalent means.
External libraries used in systems are checked for vulnerabilities using software composition analysis (SCA) or equivalent means.
Network scanning is used to confirm that there are no open ports or services without a valid business requirement.
Tests are conducted to verify whether communication is possible across defined network boundaries, confirming segmentation aligns with design intent.
Scanning tools are used to detect misconfigurations and vulnerabilities in cloud environments and container workloads.
Source code review is conducted following discovery or report of critical or notably significant vulnerabilities, and the need for a specific response is evaluated and documented.
Scans and code reviews by other developers (peer review) are conducted prior to each release.
Vulnerability scans are conducted at least annually for all in-scope systems to identify and address vulnerabilities, with results tracked through remediation closure.
Vulnerability scans are conducted following discovery or report of vulnerabilities relevant to MCNA's environment (e.g., new CVE in an in-use component, vendor advisory).

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Most recent vulnerability scan reports across in-scope categories (SAST, DAST, SCA, network, cloud, container).
Remediation tracking from finding to closure with date stamps.
Records of triggered scans following CVE disclosures or advisories.
Pre-release scan and peer-review records for systems in active development.

controls.title: Planning for Business Continuity with IT Considerations (IT-BCP, etc.)
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA identifies the IT systems essential to its business operations and prepares for their continuation and early recovery in the event of an accident, natural disaster, or cyber incident. It establishes the planning, recovery objectives, and exercise practices that make IT business continuity (IT-BCP) defensible against audit and operationally usable in a real event.
controls.cadence: Cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: Reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Extended outages of critical systems (ERP, production-floor, finance) with no defensible recovery path, causing material business interruption. Inability to meet customer commitments and contractual service levels following an accident, disaster, or cyber event. Regulatory and audit findings from NOF Corporate, external auditors, or insurers when continuity plans, RPO/RTO/MTD values, or test evidence cannot be produced on request. Reputational and financial harm if recovery decisions are improvised rather than executed against an approved and exercised plan.

clauses.group_name: Identification of Critical Systems and Recovery Objectives
clauses.clause_text: Important systems requiring continuity and fast recovery in the event of an incident or disaster are identified, and priority gradations (recovery levels) are assigned.

clauses.group_name: Identification of Critical Systems and Recovery Objectives
clauses.clause_text: Important systems essential to core business functions are identified, including ERP (Macola), production-floor systems, finance, EHS, and customer-facing capabilities.

clauses.group_name: Identification of Critical Systems and Recovery Objectives
clauses.clause_text: Maximum tolerable downtime (MTD) is defined for each in-scope system.

clauses.group_name: Identification of Critical Systems and Recovery Objectives
clauses.clause_text: Recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) are defined for each in-scope system, consistent with the priority gradation under clause 18-1.1.
Response guidelines or manuals — covering procedures to be performed in the event of an accident or disaster — are prepared and maintained, including current contact lists.
A response and recovery plan is established for use at the time of an accident or disaster, with named owners for each step.
Criteria for triggering the plan are defined and approved, eliminating ambiguity over when to invoke it.

Contact lists, role assignments, and emergency communication channels — both inside and outside the organization (NOF Corporate, DIS Computers, regulators, key customers, vendors) — are prepared and kept current.
Information processing facilities are configured with sufficient redundancy to meet defined availability targets.
Use of cloud or remote data center capacity is considered to distribute IT environments across regions and increase resilience against region-specific disasters.
Disaster and accident drills are conducted at least annually, and readiness is reviewed against drill results.
Response plans and recovery plans are tested at least annually and after material change.
Plans are reviewed and revised based on issues identified during tests and during actual recovery events, with corrective actions tracked to closure.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current inventory of in-scope systems with priority gradations and RPO/RTO/MTD values.
Most recent response and recovery plan with revision history.
Most recent drill or exercise after-action report and corrective-action tracker.
Contact lists and emergency communication channel records.

controls.title: Establishing and Disseminating Incident Response Policy – Detection and Initial Response
controls.overview: This standard defines MCNA's policy for incident detection and initial response — including the First Report and its communication. It establishes how a suspected event becomes a classified incident, who is notified, and how the response is initiated.
controls.cadence: Cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: Reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Delayed or missed detection of cyber events, allowing attackers to dwell, expand access, or exfiltrate data before MCNA responds. Inconsistent or improvised stakeholder notification, breaching contractual, regulatory, or NOF Corporate reporting obligations. Inability to demonstrate to auditors, customers, or insurers that MCNA has an approved, communicated, and exercised detection policy. Material financial, regulatory, and reputational harm from incidents that escalate due to absent or unclear escalation criteria.

clauses.clause_text: A policy addressing detection and initial response is defined as part of the MCNA incident response policy (or procedure/protocol).
Potential incident types are identified, including unauthorized access, malware infection, internal fraud, data exfiltration, and denial-of-service events.
Criteria are established for determining whether a suspected event is classified as an incident, for assessing its level of impact, and for setting the response priority.
Management escalation criteria are established, defining the threshold and routing at which an incident is escalated to the IT-MIS Director, CFO, and CEO.
A communication flow to each stakeholder is established for use when an incident occurs, and the contact-making process is systematized so that no notification depends on improvisation.
Business partners and customers are notified about incidents in line with contractual obligations, MCNA policy, and applicable regulation.
Standards for disclosure to external parties are established, and disclosure is performed in accordance with those standards.
Incident information and attacker details (tactics, techniques, procedures) are shared with public agencies and information-sharing forums where appropriate and lawful.
The detection and initial-response policy is approved by executive management (CFO and CEO) and communicated to concerned parties and stakeholders.
Roles for specialized response activities are defined; responsibilities of system administrators, network administrators, and other named operators are documented.
The detection and initial-response policy is communicated to internal and external stakeholders, with acknowledgement of roles and reporting flows recorded.
The detection and initial-response policy is reviewed at least annually; reviews incorporate challenges, issues, and lessons learned identified while executing the policy.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current detection and initial-response policy with executive approval signature.
Acknowledgement records from internal staff and external partners.
Most recent annual review minutes and lessons-learned tracker.
Stakeholder communication flow chart with current contact information.

controls.title: Establishing and Disseminating Incident Response Policy – Recovery and Improvement
controls.overview: This standard defines MCNA's policy for incident recovery and improvement — covering the Second Report (First Follow-up) and all subsequent reporting. It establishes how MCNA returns systems to normal operation, prevents recurrence, and disseminates findings.
controls.cadence: Cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: Reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Premature return to production using compromised data or unverified systems, allowing re-infection or persistent attacker presence. Recurrence of the same incident class because root-cause analysis and corrective actions were not formalized or tracked to closure. Breach of contractual, regulatory, or NOF Corporate disclosure obligations through inconsistent or untimely external communication. Loss of audit and insurance defensibility when post-incident reports, integrity-test records, and lessons-learned trackers cannot be produced on request.

clauses.clause_text: Policies, procedures, or protocols addressing recovery and improvement (including the prevention of recurrence) after incidents are defined and maintained.
Policy is established for identifying the circumstances of the event, the attack methods, and the root cause(s).
The extent and range of impact is verified, including checking for compromise of other assets that share infrastructure, accounts, or data with the affected system.
Responses to prevent the spread of damage (containment) and to eliminate the cause of damage (root-cause eradication) are established.
Recovery policy and the criteria for initiating recovery actions are defined and approved.
The root cause is verified as fixed, and data used for restoration is verified as showing no signs of compromise, before that data is used to restore systems.
Restored systems are tested for integrity before being returned to production use.
Standards for disclosure to external parties are established, and disclosure is performed in accordance with those standards.
Recovery actions and their progress are communicated to external stakeholders in line with disclosure standards.
Recovery actions and recurrence-prevention measures are publicly disclosed where required by law, contract, or MCNA policy.
For every incident, incident details and the response actions taken are documented in a contemporaneous record.
A post-incident report is prepared summarizing the incident details, response actions, recovery actions, and lessons learned.
Information-security continuity, redundancy, and availability are confirmed to be maintained even in the event of system overload or cyber attack.
The recovery and improvement policy is approved by executive management (CFO and CEO) and communicated to concerned parties and stakeholders.
Roles for specialized recovery activities are defined; responsibilities of system administrators, network administrators, and other named operators are documented.
The recovery and improvement policy is communicated to internal and external stakeholders, with acknowledgement of roles and reporting flows recorded.
The recovery and improvement policy is reviewed at least annually; reviews incorporate challenges, issues, and lessons learned identified while executing the policy.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current recovery and improvement policy with executive approval signature.
Most recent post-incident reports and lessons-learned tracker.
Acknowledgement records from internal staff and external partners.
Records of integrity testing prior to production restoration.

controls.title: Establishing and Disseminating Incident Response Procedures or Operating Guidance
controls.overview: This standard defines the operational procedures that translate MCNA's incident-response policy into specific, executable steps. It covers impact assessment, initial and tentative response, permanent response, forensic acquisition, automation, and per-incident-type playbooks.
controls.cadence: Cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: Reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: Cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Slower or inconsistent containment when responders work from memory rather than approved playbooks, increasing dwell time and impact. Forensic evidence loss or inadmissibility because acquisition, chain-of-custody, or access-restriction controls were not followed. Audit and insurance findings when per-incident-type procedures, automation evidence, or post-incident reviews cannot be produced. Failure to incorporate lessons learned, causing the same procedural defects to recur incident after incident.

clauses.clause_text: Specific response procedures are established for assessing incident impact, initial response, tentative response, permanent response, and preventive measures.
The established response procedures are approved by site leadership and upper management and communicated to all concerned parties (including all RACI parties).
To enable rapid forensic investigation, detailed log and system information is acquired in real time using EDR or equivalent capability, in cooperation with analysts.
Data collected during forensic investigations is protected from tampering, forging, modification, and unauthorized access so that it remains usable for analysis and as evidence.
Procedures that can be automated are automated; a combination of automatic and manual response is used to respond to incidents quickly.
Procedures specific to each incident type — fraud, malware, internal fraud, ransomware, business email compromise, etc. — are created and maintained.
The response procedures are reviewed at least annually.
A post-incident review is performed after each occurrence; results are used to revise procedures and to implement additional security measures where indicated.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current incident-response procedure set with executive approval.
Per-incident-type playbooks with revision dates.
Post-incident reviews and corrective-action tracker.
Records of evidence-handling controls (EDR retention, chain-of-custody, access restrictions).

controls.title: Formation of Incident Response Teams
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA composes the team responsible for handling incidents, including the skills required, the roles assigned during emergencies and steady-state, and the availability expected of the team.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Unclear roles and handoffs that delay or fragment incident response. Gaps in 24x365 coverage that leave MCNA without response capability outside business hours. Single points of failure when individual team members are absent, depart, or are unavailable. Audit findings against Secure SketCH 19-4 and the parent IT and Information Systems Security Policy.

clauses.clause_text: The skills necessary to conduct root-cause analysis, to respond to incidents, and to study measures preventing recurrence are understood and formulated, and team members are selected on that basis.

An incident-response flow diagram or chart is created showing not only the technical responder but also all relevant teams and departments — finance, HR (Legal), operations, external public-relations support, NOF Corporate liaison, and external partners.
The roles and responsibilities of stakeholders are clarified for both event time (during an incident) and steady state, and recorded so that handoffs do not depend on individual memory.
The incident-response team is available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, physically or remotely, achieved through MCNA personnel and DIS Computers’ contracted SOC capability.
The organization’s members, their roles, and their responsibilities are reviewed at least annually and updated on personnel change.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current incident-response flow diagram with named roles.
Skills matrix and current team roster (MCNA and DIS).
24x365 coverage attestation from DIS Computers.
Most recent annual review minutes.

controls.title: Training the Incident Response Teams
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA trains its incident-response teams through tabletop and live simulations, ensuring that response procedures are understood, practiced, and refined against current threat scenarios.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Response procedures that look correct on paper but fail under live conditions. Slower containment, longer downtime, and greater impact when teams have not rehearsed against current threat scenarios. Training gaps that recur because findings are not fed back into procedures. Audit findings against Secure SketCH 20-1 and the parent IT and Information Systems Security Policy.

clauses.clause_text: Reviews of response procedures are conducted with the incident-response teams, deployed against each risk scenario (e.g., malware infection using business email compromise, ransomware, insider fraud, third-party compromise, denial-of-service), to identify areas for improvement.
Incident-response training is conducted for the incident-response team, and the training content is documented and retained as audit evidence.
Tabletop or live training for incident response is conducted for each risk scenario, with documented objectives, participants, and outcomes.
A training environment is prepared as needed to minimize the impact on production operations.
Recorded training content is reviewed; incident-response policies and procedures are revised based on findings.
Training content is reviewed and regular training is conducted to account for the latest threats — at minimum annually, with additional sessions following material changes in the threat landscape.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Current training plan and risk-scenario list.
Records of tabletop and live training sessions with participants and outcomes.
After-action reports and revisions to incident-response procedures.
Annual training calendar with completion records.

controls.title: Cross-Functional Incident Response Training
controls.overview: This standard defines how MCNA conducts incident-response training that extends beyond the incident-response team to all relevant departments and to involved external parties — building the cross-functional cooperation that real incidents demand.
controls.cadence: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.reviewer: IT-MIS Director, with input from DIS Computers, and approval from the CFO.
controls.status_description: At least annually, with out-of-cycle reviews triggered by the events listed below.
controls.insufficient_measures_risks: Failure to implement and maintain this standard exposes MCNA to: Cross-functional handoffs that break down during real incidents because non-IT departments have not rehearsed their role. External partners and vendors that are not aligned with MCNA’s response procedures. Communications, legal, and finance decisions that delay containment because they were not exercised in advance. Audit findings against Secure SketCH 20-2 and the parent IT and Information Systems Security Policy.

clauses.clause_text: Cross-functional reviews are conducted with participants from teams, functions, and departments beyond the incident-response team, and involve organizational leadership in scenario walkthroughs.
Incident-response training is conducted for internal departments and staff in addition to the incident-response team, and the training content is documented.
Tabletop exercises or live/hands-on trainings for incident response are conducted for each risk scenario, scoped to the cross-functional audience.
A training environment is prepared as needed to minimize the impact on production operations.
Recorded training content is reviewed, and incident-response policies and procedures are revised based on findings.

When shortcomings are identified, findings are not limited to the incident-response team — improvements involving all concerned teams (including teams that should be added to the response roster, or whose handoffs need clarification) are recorded and tracked.
Training is conducted involving important external vendors, contractors, and other relevant third parties (including DIS Computers and key suppliers) as needed.

Training content is reviewed and regular training is conducted to account for the latest threats — at minimum annually, with additional sessions when the threat landscape or organizational structure changes materially.

audit_evidence_items.item_text: Cross-functional training calendar and participant rosters.
After-action reports identifying cross-functional improvements.
Records of training sessions involving external vendors and contractors.
Revisions to incident-response policies traceable to training findings.
